definition_en: a hollow container used to give shape to soft material; a growth of fungus on food or surfaces; to press material into a shape, or to influence how a person develops
core_image: 湿泥被按进木框，倒扣出来就是一只碗的形状
scene: 陶艺课上，师傅把湿泥按进木框里，再倒扣在架上，一排碗的雏形就出来了。 She pressed the clay into a wooden mold and left it to dry.
sceneCN: 这里 mold 是「模具、模子」（第 1 个义项：让软材料成形的凹型容器）；句意为她把陶土按进木模具，然后放在一旁晾干。画面里能想见：木框、湿泥、倒扣出来的碗坯。

pos.zh: 塑造；使成形；用模具制作；影响（性格）

derivatives.zh: 由 mold 加 -ing 构成，义为「模制品；建筑上的线脚」
由 mold 加 -y 构成，义为「发霉的；有霉味的」
由 mold 加 -able 构成，义为「可塑的；容易成形的」
由 mold 加 -er 构成，义为「制模工」

senses.title: A hollow container that gives shape to soft material
senses.definition: a hollow container with a particular shape, into which soft material is pressed so that it takes that shape
senses.definitionCN: 具有特定形状的空心容器，把软材料压进去，材料就随之成型
senses.example: She pressed the clay into a wooden mold and left it to dry.
senses.exampleCN: 她把陶土按进木模具，然后放在一旁晾干。
senses.why: Latin modulus meant a small measure, and a mould is exactly a measured cavity: the size of the object is fixed before the material arrives.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modulus 意为「小尺度」，而模子正是一个量好的空腔：材料还没进去，成品的尺寸就已经定死了。

senses.title: A growth of fungus on food or damp surfaces
senses.definition: a soft green, grey or white fungus that grows on food or on damp walls and leather
senses.definitionCN: 长在食物、潮湿墙面或皮革上的灰绿、灰白软质真菌
senses.example: There was black mold along the bathroom tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 浴室瓷砖的缝隙里长着黑霉。
senses.why: This sense is a different word in origin; it is usually linked to an old word for loose earth, because mould grows where things sit damp and begin to break down.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项在词源上是另一个词，一般认为与表示「松软泥土」的古词有关，因为霉总是长在潮湿、开始腐烂的东西上。

senses.title: To press material into a shape
senses.definition: to press a soft substance into a particular shape, by hand or with a container
senses.definitionCN: 用手或容器把柔软的物质压成某个形状
senses.example: He molded the wet sand into a small castle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把湿沙子塑成一座小城堡。
senses.why: If the mould is the measured cavity, the verb is the act of filling it; the word shifts from the tool to the work done with the tool.
senses.whyCN: 如果模子是量好的空腔，动词就是往里填的动作；词于是从工具转到用工具做的那件事。

senses.title: To shape a person's character or ideas
senses.definition: to influence strongly how someone's character, beliefs or habits develop
senses.definitionCN: 强烈影响某人的性格、信念或习惯如何发展
senses.example: School molded her into a careful reader.
senses.exampleCN: 学校把她培养成了一个细心的读书人。
senses.why: A child is soft material in the hands of family and teachers, so the same verb for pressing clay into a mould is used for forming a mind.
senses.whyCN: 孩子在家和老师手里就是软的材料，于是那个「把泥按进模子」的动词被借来形容心智的形成。

intro.en: Mold has two histories: the shaping word runs back to a Latin measure, while the fungus word is usually traced to an old word for earth.
intro.cn: mold 有两段来历：表示「成形」的那个词可追到拉丁语的尺度，表示「霉」的那个词一般认为来自表示泥土的古词。

items.en: Modulus was a small measure, a diminutive of modus, and it named the fixed size against which things were checked.
items.cn: modulus 是「小尺度」，由 modus 缩成，指用来核对事物的既定尺寸。

items.en: Old French modle took the word as a pattern or model, the shape a finished object should follow.
items.cn: 古法语把词写作 modle，指样板或模型，即成品应当照着做的形状。

items.en: Middle English used mold for the hollow pattern that potters and metal workers filled with their material.
items.cn: 中古英语用 mold 指陶工与金属工匠往里填料的空心模范。

items.en: The fungus sense is generally connected with Old English molde, loose earth; its exact development is uncertain, and dictionaries treat it as a separate word.
items.cn: 霉的义项一般认为与古英语 molde（松软泥土）有关，其确切演变不确定，词典把它当作另一个词处理。

items.en: Modern English keeps both senses in one spelling mold in American use, while British use writes mould; the extra u is usually explained as a later spelling habit.
items.cn: 现代英语在美式拼写里把两个义项都写成 mold，英式写 mould；多出来的 u 一般被解释为后来的拼写习惯。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers spellings and relatives built on the shaping word; the near-meaning group gathers words for casting, forming and fungus growth.
note.cn: 形近组收「成形」这个词上的拼写与同族词；近义组收表示浇铸、成形与霉菌生长的词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of mold, used for both the container and the fungus.
entries.definitionCN: mold 的英式拼写，模具与霉两个义项都用它。

entries.definition: Something made in a mold, or a shaped strip along a wall.
entries.definitionCN: 模制出来的东西，或墙面上的线脚。

entries.definition: Covered with or tasting of mold.
Soft enough to be pressed into a shape.
entries.definitionCN: 软到可以被压成形的；可塑的。

entries.definition: A small measure in Latin, the source of mold and of module.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中的「小尺度」，是 mold 与 module 的来源。

entries.definition: To pour melted metal or other material into a mold.
entries.definitionCN: 把熔化的金属等材料浇进模子。

entries.definition: To give something a particular form.
entries.definitionCN: 给某物一个特定的形状。

entries.definition: To make or develop into a particular shape or arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 使成为或发展成某种形状、结构。

entries.definition: A plant-like growth such as mold, mildew or mushroom.
entries.definitionCN: 霉、白粉病或蘑菇一类近似植物的生长物。

normalIntro.en: One spelling carries a family about measured cavities and a separate word about damp growth; both are worth keeping apart in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个拼写承载着「量好的空腔」这一词族，也承载着另一个表示潮湿生长的词；记忆时要把两者分开。

normal.en: Modulus is Latin for a small measure, so a mold is a cavity whose size was decided in advance.
normal.cn: modulus 是拉丁语的「小尺度」，所以模子就是尺寸事先定好的空腔。

normal.en: Molding adds -ing: the thing that comes out of the mold, or the shaped strip on a wall.
normal.cn: molding 加 -ing：从模子里出来的东西，或墙上成形的线脚。

normal.en: Moldy adds -y: full of mold, therefore spoiled and smelling of damp.
normal.cn: moldy 加 -y：长满霉，因此坏了、带着潮味。

normal.en: Moldable adds -able: able to take a shape, the way wet clay can.
normal.cn: moldable 加 -able：能够被塑成形状，就像湿陶土那样。

normal.en: British mould and American mold differ only in the u, as with colour and color.
normal.cn: 英式 mould 与美式 mold 只差一个 u，和 colour 与 color 的情况一样。

abstract.en: A mold is a promise made before the material arrives: the outcome is already written in the cavity.
abstract.cn: 模子是材料到来之前就许下的承诺：结果已经写在空腔里。

abstract.en: Shaping a child and shaping clay use one verb because both require gentle, repeated pressure.
abstract.cn: 塑造孩子与塑造陶土共用一个动词，因为两者都需要温和而反复的按压。

abstract.en: Mold the fungus is a reminder that soft, damp places quietly rewrite whatever rests in them.
abstract.cn: 表示霉的 mold 提醒人：柔软潮湿的地方会悄悄改写停放在那里的东西。

examples.en: She pressed the clay into a wooden mold and left it to dry.
examples.cn: 她把陶土按进木模具，然后放在一旁晾干。

examples.en: There was black mold along the bathroom tiles.
examples.cn: 浴室瓷砖的缝隙里长着黑霉。

examples.en: School molded her into a careful reader.
examples.cn: 学校把她培养成了一个细心的读书人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸的」——用手摸摸湿泥，再按进框里；mold 就是模子、塑形。

root: 表示「成形」的 mold 来自拉丁语 modulus（小尺度，modus 的指小形式），经古法语 modle 进入英语；表示「霉」的义项一般认为另出自古英语 molde（泥土），来源不完全确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a measured hollow that decides a shape; from it come the container, the act of pressing, and the shaping of a mind, while the fungus sense is a separate old word that shares the spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个决定形状的量好空腔；由此分出容器、按压动作与心智的塑造，而表示霉的义项是共用拼写的另一个古词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wet clay pressed into a wooden frame and turned out as a bowl.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿泥被按进木框，倒扣出来就是一只碗。

branches.en: rows of wooden frames waiting for clay
branches.cn: 一排等着装泥的木框

branches.en: a green patch spreading over old bread
branches.cn: 旧面包上蔓延的绿斑

branches.en: a hand pressing sand into a castle
branches.cn: 一只手把沙子压成城堡

branches.en: a teacher steadying a child's reading habit
branches.cn: 老师一点点扶正孩子的读书习惯

branches.en: a metal spoon lifted out of a sand mold
branches.cn: 从砂模里取出的金属勺

intro.en: A Latin measure word, its diminutive, a French pattern word and English endings from -ing to im- hold the shaping family together; the fungus sense sits outside it.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语尺度词、它的指小形式、一个法语「样板」词，加上从 -ing 到 im- 的英语词尾，撑起了「成形」这一族；表示霉的义项在这一族之外。

latinIntro.en: Modus and its diminutive modulus belong to the Latin vocabulary of measuring; the fungus sense has no Latin cognate and is left out of this list.
latinIntro.cn: modus 及其指小形式 modulus 属于拉丁语「量度」词汇；表示霉的义项没有拉丁同族词，因此不列入。

definition_zh: 蜡；蜂蜡；蜡状物；（月亮）渐圆；增大
definition_en: a soft yellowish substance made by bees or used for polishing, and also the act of growing larger, as the moon does
core_image: 一支蜡烛被点燃，火苗边上慢慢淌下一道温热的蜡泪
scene: 桌上那支旧蜡烛烧到一半，融化的蜡顺着铜盘边缘凝成一圈淡黄。 By midnight the candle had melted into a pool of wax on the brass plate.
sceneCN: 这里 wax 是「蜡」（第 1 个义项：蜜蜂或工业制成的柔软黄色物质）；句意为到午夜时，蜡烛已经化成一摊蜡留在铜盘上。火苗边淌下的那一道蜡泪就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The substance of candles
senses.definition: a soft pale substance that melts easily and is used for candles, polish and seals
senses.definitionCN: 一种柔软、颜色浅、容易熔化的物质，用来做蜡烛、上光剂与封蜡
senses.example: The wax from the candle ran down onto the brass plate.
senses.exampleCN: 蜡烛的蜡淌下来，落在铜盘上。
senses.why: The earliest sense in English is the material itself, taken from the substance bees build with.
senses.whyCN: 英语里最古老的意思是这种材料本身，取自蜜蜂筑巢所用的东西。

senses.title: The material bees build with
senses.definition: the substance that bees produce and use to build the cells of their hive
senses.definitionCN: 蜜蜂分泌并用它筑成蜂巢小格的那种物质
senses.example: The beekeeper scraped the wax off the frames and saved it for polish.
senses.exampleCN: 养蜂人把蜂蜡从框架上刮下来，留着做上光剂。
senses.why: Because honeycomb was the everyday source, the plain word first meant this animal product.
senses.whyCN: 由于蜂巢是日常来源，这个普通名词最初就指这种动物产物。

senses.title: A likeness made of wax
senses.definition: a figure of a person modelled in wax, as in a museum
senses.definitionCN: 用蜡塑成的人像，常见于蜡像馆
senses.example: Visitors queue to photograph the wax figures in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 参观者排队在大厅里给蜡像拍照。
senses.why: A material soft enough to model gave English a short way to name the imitation itself.
senses.whyCN: 一种软到可以塑形的材料，让英语有了指称仿制人像的简便说法。

senses.title: To grow larger, as the moon
senses.definition: of the moon, to show more of its lit face night after night
senses.definitionCN: 指月亮一夜夜露出更多被照亮的表面
senses.example: The moon will wax for another week before it is full.
senses.exampleCN: 月亮还会再圆上一个星期才到满月。
senses.why: This growth sense comes from a different Old English verb meaning to increase, which now shares the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这一「增长」义来自另一个古英语动词，意为增多，如今与蜡共用拼写。

senses.title: To increase or grow stronger
senses.definition: to become larger, stronger or more intense, in literary or formal use
senses.definitionCN: 在书面或正式用法中指变大、变强或变得更为强烈
senses.example: Interest in the old songs waxed again after the film appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 电影上映之后，人们对那些老歌的兴趣再度高涨。
senses.why: From the moon the verb spreads to anything that steadily increases, and usually pairs with wane.
senses.whyCN: 从月亮出发，这个动词扩展到一切稳步增长的事物，且常与 wane 成对使用。

senses.title: To apply wax to a surface
senses.definition: to rub wax onto a surface in order to polish or protect it
senses.definitionCN: 把蜡擦到表面上，使其光亮或受到保护
senses.example: He waxed the wooden floor until it shone.
senses.exampleCN: 他把木地板打了蜡，直到它发亮。
senses.why: Once the noun named the stuff, the verb could simply mean putting it on things.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指称这种材料，动词就可以直接表示把它涂上去。

intro.en: Wax as a substance goes back to Old English weax, and the verb meaning to grow is a separate Old English word that later fell into the same spelling.
intro.cn: 表示物质的 wax 可上溯到古英语 weax；表示「增长」的动词则是另一个古英语词，后来拼写并入了一处。

items.en: Weax named the material of honeycomb, a word shared with the other old Germanic tongues.
items.cn: weax 指蜂巢的材料，这个词与其他古老日耳曼语言共有一个来源。

items.en: The Germanic root is related to words for weaving, since bees appear to weave their cells.
items.cn: 这一日耳曼词根与「编织」有关，因为在人看来蜜蜂像是在把巢房编出来。

items.en: A separate verb weaxan meant to grow or increase, and it described the moon as well as plants.
items.cn: 另有一个独立的动词 weaxan，意为生长、增多，既用于植物也用于月亮。

items.en: The two words came to be written alike, so wax meant both the substance and the growing.
items.cn: 两个词的写法逐渐趋同，于是 wax 同时表示材料与增长。

items.en: English kept the moon phrase wax and wane and added the everyday verb to wax a floor.
items.cn: 英语保留了 wax and wane 这一月亮短语，又添出「给地板打蜡」这样的日常动词。

note.en: The first group is built on the same material, the second on the idea of growing.
note.cn: 第一组来自同一种材料，第二组来自「增长」这一概念。

entries.definition: Like wax in texture or colour.
Made of wax, or pale as wax.
A figure or ornament made of wax.
The wax produced by honeybees.
To rub a surface until it shines, with or without wax.
The object chiefly made of this material.
To become larger, the plain verb behind the moon sense.
To increase in size, often more suddenly.

normalIntro.en: Hold the two lives of wax apart: one is a soft yellow material, the other is steady growth.
normalIntro.cn: 把 wax 的两副面孔分开记：一面是柔软的黄色材料，一面是稳步的增长。

normal.en: Wax on a candle melts; wax on a floor is rubbed in.
normal.cn: 蜡烛上的蜡会熔化，地板上的蜡是被擦进去的。

normal.en: Beeswax is the wax that bees make.
normal.cn: beeswax 就是蜜蜂做的那种蜡。

normal.en: Wax and wane is the moon pair; wax alone means to grow.
normal.cn: wax and wane 是月亮的一对，单独的 wax 意为增长。

normal.en: A wax figure is a person copied in wax.
normal.cn: wax figure 是用蜡复制出来的人。

normal.en: To wax a floor is to put the noun onto the floor.
normal.cn: wax a floor 就是把名词蜡涂到地板上。

abstract.en: Picture a flame leaning sideways as a drop slides down.
abstract.cn: 想火苗被压得歪一点，一滴蜡正往下滑。

abstract.en: Feel the floor turn smooth under the cloth.
abstract.cn: 感受地板在布下面变得光滑。

abstract.en: See a thin bright edge on the moon getting wider.
abstract.cn: 看月亮那道细细的亮边一点点变宽。

examples.en: The wax figures in the museum are replaced every few years.
examples.cn: 博物馆里的蜡像每隔几年就会更换。

examples.en: She waxed the old table until the grain stood out.
examples.cn: 她给旧桌子打了蜡，木纹清晰起来。

examples.en: Public anger waxed as the weeks passed.
examples.cn: 随着一周周过去，公众的愤怒越来越大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挖克斯」——挖克斯老头守着一支蜡烛，蜡一点点淌下来，月亮也一点点圆起来。

root: 古英语 weax（蜂蜡，与「编织」词根相关）+ 古英语 weaxan（生长、增多）；同源词有 waxy、beeswax。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a material, spreads to things made of it, and is joined by an older verb of growing that the spelling swallowed.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初指一种材料，扩展到用它做成的东西，又并入了一个更古老的「生长」动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of soft yellow wax sliding down a candle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴柔软的黄色蜡顺着蜡烛滑落。

branches.en: The material branch: candles and the honeycomb it comes from.
branches.cn: 材料分支：蜡烛与它来源的蜂巢。

branches.en: The copy branch: figures modelled from the same stuff.
branches.cn: 仿制分支：用同一种材料塑出的人像。

branches.en: The growth branch: a moon filling out and anger rising.
branches.cn: 增长分支：月亮渐圆与怒气渐涨。

branches.en: The doing branch: rubbing the noun onto wood.
branches.cn: 动作分支：把名词蜡擦到木头上。

branches.en: The source branch: what the bees leave in the hive.
branches.cn: 来源分支：蜜蜂留在蜂巢里的东西。

intro.en: Wax is a native Germanic word, so the affixes here are mostly compounds and endings that grew in English.
intro.cn: wax 是本土日耳曼词，所以这里的构词主要是英语内部长出的复合与词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin verb for wax, so the Latin table stands empty and only the native roots are shown.
latinIntro.cn: wax 没有对应的拉丁动词，故拉丁表留空，只保留本土词根。

items.example: It is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: 这是最早有记录的形式。
它出现在 candle wax 里。

definition_zh: 升（公制容量单位，等于一立方分米）；一升的量
definition_en: a metric unit of volume equal to one cubic decimetre, or the amount of liquid that such a unit contains
core_image: 一只透明量杯里，水正好停在刻着升的那一道线上
scene: 厨房的台面上放着一只透明量杯，水正好停在刻线处。 She poured a litre of milk into the jug and set it in the fridge.
sceneCN: 这里 litre 是「升」（第 1 个义项：公制容量单位）；句意为她把一升牛奶倒进壶里放进冰箱。图中可辨识物件：透明量杯、刻线、牛奶壶。

derivatives.zh: litre 的美式拼写，含义相同，义为「升」
由 litre 加表示「千分之一」的 milli- 构成，义为「毫升」
由 litre 加表示「千」的 kilo- 构成，义为「千升」

senses.title: A metric unit of volume
senses.definition: a metric unit of volume equal to one cubic decimetre, used for measuring liquids and sometimes grain
senses.definitionCN: 等于一立方分米的公制容量单位，用来计量液体，有时也计量谷物
senses.example: The bottle holds one litre of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这只瓶子能装一升水。
senses.why: The metric system was designed in France, where an older capacity measure called litron supplied the name; the unit was fixed at one cubic decimetre and travelled with the system.
senses.whyCN: 公制在法国设计，当地一种旧的容量单位 litron 提供了名字；这个单位被定为一立方分米，随后随公制传开。

senses.title: The amount contained in one litre
senses.definition: the quantity of liquid or other substance that fills a container of one litre
senses.definitionCN: 装满一升容器所需的液体或其他物质的量
senses.example: She poured a litre of milk into the jug.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一升牛奶倒进壶里。
senses.why: A fixed unit can stand for the quantity it measures: people buy a litre as readily as they buy a metre, so the unit name becomes the name of the amount.
senses.whyCN: 固定的单位可以代替它所量的数量：人们买一升，就像买一米那样自然，于是单位名也成了数量的名字。

intro.en: Litre comes from a French capacity measure, which in turn goes back through Latin to a Greek unit of weight whose earlier origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: litre 来自法国的一种容量单位，再经拉丁语上溯到希腊的一种重量单位，而它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Greek litra named a Sicilian unit of weight and later a coin; its ultimate origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 litra 指西西里的一种重量单位，后来也指钱币；它最终的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin borrowed litra as a name for a small weight or measure, and medieval Latin used it for a measure of capacity.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 litra，指一种小重量或小量具；中世纪拉丁语用它指容量单位。

items.en: Old French litron named a measure of capacity, and French formed litre from it when the metric system was being designed.
items.cn: 古法语 litron 指一种容量单位；法国在设计公制时由它造出了 litre。

items.en: English adopted litre in the nineteenth century together with the metric system and kept the French spelling with -re.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语随公制一起借入 litre，并保留了法语中以 -re 结尾的拼写。

items.en: Modern English uses litre in British spelling and liter in American spelling; both name the same metric unit.
items.cn: 现代英语在英式拼写中用 litre，在美式拼写中用 liter；两者指的是同一个公制单位。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers spellings and multiples of the metric unit; the near-meaning group gathers other units used to measure volume.
note.cn: 形近组收这个公制单位的拼写变体与倍数单位；近义组收其他用来计量体积的单位。

entries.definition: The American spelling of litre, naming the same unit.
entries.definitionCN: litre 的美式拼写，指的是同一个单位。

entries.definition: One thousandth of a litre.
One thousand litres.
An old French measure of capacity that gave the name litre.
entries.definitionCN: 法国旧时的容量单位，litre 的名字由它而来。

entries.definition: A larger unit of volume used in Britain and America.
entries.definitionCN: 加仑；英美使用的一种较大容量单位。

entries.definition: A unit of volume used for milk and beer, about half a quart.
entries.definitionCN: 品脱；用来量牛奶和啤酒的容量单位，约半夸脱。

entries.definition: A unit of volume equal to two pints.
entries.definitionCN: 夸脱；等于两品脱的容量单位。

entries.definition: A unit of volume equal to one millilitre.
entries.definitionCN: 立方厘米；等于一毫升的容量单位。

normalIntro.en: The word is a French name for a capacity measure, and its family keeps returning to prefixes that multiply and divide the unit.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是法语中一个容量单位的名字，它的同族词反复回到把该单位成倍放大或缩小的前缀。

normal.en: The metric system was built in France, and litre comes from a French measure called litron.
normal.cn: 公制在法国建立，litre 则来自法国一种叫 litron 的量具。

normal.en: Greek litra first named a weight, so the unit began as something weighed rather than something poured.
normal.cn: 希腊语 litra 最初指重量，所以这个单位最早是称出来的，而不是倒出来的。

normal.en: Milli- means a thousandth, so a millilitre is one thousandth of a litre.
normal.cn: milli- 表示千分之一，所以 millilitre 是一升的千分之一。

normal.en: Kilo- means a thousand, so a kilolitre is a thousand litres.
normal.cn: kilo- 表示千，所以 kilolitre 是一千升。

normal.en: The British write litre and Americans write liter, just as theatre and theater differ.
normal.cn: 英国人写 litre，美国人写 liter，就像 theatre 与 theater 的差别一样。

abstract.en: A litre is a cube ten centimetres on each side, a volume you can almost hold in two hands.
abstract.cn: 一升是边长十厘米的立方体，一个几乎能捧在双手里的体积。

abstract.en: The same name can mean the unit and the amount, because measuring and the thing measured are hard to separate.
abstract.cn: 同一个名字既可以指单位，也可以指数量，因为计量行为与被量的东西很难分开。

abstract.en: Every country that sells petrol by the litre is using a measure invented in a French laboratory.
abstract.cn: 每个按升卖汽油的国家，用的都是法国实验室里发明出来的量法。

examples.en: The bottle holds one litre of water.
examples.cn: 这只瓶子能装一升水。

examples.en: She poured a litre of milk into the jug.
examples.cn: 她把一升牛奶倒进壶里。

examples.en: Fuel is sold by the litre at most stations in Europe.
examples.cn: 欧洲多数加油站的燃料按升出售。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离特」——离开特定的刻度，就是一升的界线；litre 是升。

root: 希腊语 litra（一种重量单位、钱币）→ 拉丁语 litra（小重量、容量单位）→ 古法语 litron（容量单位）→ 法语 litre → 英语 litre；同族词多与公制容量有关，更早的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a fixed metric volume; the senses divide into the unit itself and the amount that one unit contains.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个固定的公制体积；义项由此分出单位本身，以及一个单位所装的量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water in a clear measuring jug stopping exactly at the litre mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：透明量杯里的水正好停在标着升的那道刻线上。

branches.en: a measuring jug filled to the marked line
branches.cn: 量杯里的水正好到刻线

branches.en: a milk carton stamped with its volume
branches.cn: 牛奶盒上印着容量

branches.en: a bottle tipped over a glass
branches.cn: 瓶子往杯里倒出一升的量

branches.en: a petrol pump counting litres
branches.cn: 加油枪在按升计数

branches.en: a laboratory beaker on a bench
branches.cn: 实验台上的一只烧杯

intro.en: A Greek weight name, its Latin borrowing, a French measure and French prefix forms carry litre from an old balance to the petrol pump.
intro.cn: 一个希腊重量名、它的拉丁借形、一个法国量具，再加法语前缀形式，把 litre 从旧时的天平带到加油枪。

latinIntro.en: Litra is a recorded Latin word, but Latin took it from Greek and its earlier origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: litra 是有记录的拉丁词，但拉丁语是从希腊语借来的，它更早的来源不确定。

items.meaning: a unit of weight, a coin

definition_zh: 出口；排放口；插座；电源接口；销路；经销店；发泄途径
definition_en: a place or pipe through which something flows out; a socket that supplies electricity; a shop or channel through which goods are sold; and a way of releasing energy or feelings
core_image: 墙根下一个半圆的排水口，水从那里流出去，汇进外面的沟
scene: 雨后的墙角积了一小片水，水沿着砖缝往低处走，最后钻进墙根那个半圆的口子。 Water poured from the outlet into the gutter.
sceneCN: 这里是「出口、排放口」（第 1 个义项：让水或气体流出去的口子）；句意为水从那个排水口流进沟里。图中可辨识物件：墙角积水、砖缝、半圆形排水口。

pos.zh: 出口；排放口；插座；电源接口；销路；经销店；发泄途径

derivatives.zh: 语源上的基础动词，古英语作 lǣtan，义为「让、放」；outlet 即「让东西出去」的地方
由 in 与 let 构成，与 outlet 方向相反，义为「入口；进水口」
由 out 与 fall 复合而成，义为「排水口；落水口」，与 outlet 义近

senses.title: An opening through which something flows out
senses.definition: an opening, pipe or channel through which water, air or another substance leaves a container, building or machine
senses.definitionCN: 让水、空气或其他物质离开容器、建筑物或机器的口子、管道或通道
senses.example: Water poured from the outlet into the gutter.
senses.exampleCN: 水从排水口流进沟里。
senses.why: Outlet is out plus let, literally a letting out: the word names the point where something is allowed to go, so its first sense is a physical opening.
senses.whyCN: outlet 是 out 加 let，字面就是「放出去」：这个词指某样东西被允许离开的那个点，所以最初的意思是一个实体的口子。

senses.title: A socket that supplies electricity
senses.definition: a socket in a wall or on a device where a plug is connected to the electricity supply
senses.definitionCN: 墙上或设备上供插头接入电源的插座
senses.example: The lamp would not work until she found another outlet.
senses.exampleCN: 她找到另一个插座，台灯才亮起来。
senses.why: Electricity is imagined as a flow, so the point where current leaves the wiring for a device borrowed the word already used for a water opening.
senses.whyCN: 电被想象成一种流，于是电流离开线路、进入电器的那一点，就借用了原本给水口子的那个词。

senses.title: A shop or channel that sells goods
senses.definition: a shop, company or channel through which goods are sold, especially one selling a manufacturer's products
senses.definitionCN: 把货物卖出去的店铺、公司或渠道，尤指销售某厂商产品的店
senses.example: The brand opened a new outlet on the edge of town.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌在城镇边缘开了一家新的经销店。
senses.why: Goods also need a way out of the warehouse, so the market where a product leaves the maker's hands took the same name, and later the shop itself was called an outlet.
senses.whyCN: 货物同样需要一条走出仓库的路，于是产品离开厂家、进入市场的那一环沿用了同一个词，后来那家店本身也被叫作 outlet。

senses.title: A way of releasing pent-up energy
senses.definition: a means of expressing or releasing strong feelings, energy or creativity that might otherwise be held in
senses.definitionCN: 把压抑的情感、精力或创造力表达、释放出去的途径
senses.example: Running became his outlet after the long working days.
senses.exampleCN: 在漫长的工作日之后，跑步成了他的发泄途径。
senses.why: When pressure has no physical opening, English extends the same image to feelings: an outlet is wherever the built-up force is finally allowed to escape.
senses.whyCN: 当压力找不到实体的口子，英语就把同一个画面挪到情绪上：凡是积起来的力量最终得以泄出的地方，都叫 outlet。

intro.en: Outlet is an English compound of out and let, where let still carries its old sense of allowing something to go; the word first named a way out for water and air.
intro.cn: outlet 是 out 与 let 的英语复合词，其中 let 仍保留「让某物走」的旧义；这个词最初指水与空气的出路。

items.en: The verb lǣtan meant to let or allow, and it supplied the second half of the compound.
items.cn: 动词 lǣtan 意为让、允许，提供了这个复合词的后半部分。

items.en: Middle English joined out and let for a place where something is let out, chiefly water or air.
items.cn: 中古英语把 out 与 let 合起来，指某物被放出去的地方，主要是水或空气。

items.en: The word was used for the mouth of a river, a drain, or any passage by which a liquid escapes.
items.cn: 这个词用来指河口、排水沟，或任何让液体流走的通道。

items.en: A further sense named the market where goods find a way out, and American usage applied the word to the socket that lets current out of a wall.
items.cn: 后来又有一义，指货物找到出路的市场；美式用法又把这个词用在让电流离开墙壁的插座上。

items.en: Modern English speaks of retail outlets, media outlets and an outlet for anger, all keeping the idea of something escaping.
items.cn: 现代英语说 retail outlets、media outlets 以及 an outlet for anger，都保留着「有东西流出去」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the let family and the parallel compounds built with out; the near-meaning group collects words for openings, supply points and markets.
note.cn: 形近组收 let 词族以及用 out 平行造出的复合词；近义组收表示「口子、供电点与市场」的词。

entries.definition: An opening through which something enters, the reverse of an outlet.
entries.definitionCN: 让东西进入的口子，与 outlet 相对；入口、进水口。

entries.definition: The place where a drain or river discharges its water.
entries.definitionCN: 排水沟或河流把水排出去的地方。

entries.definition: To allow something to happen or to go.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某事发生或让某物走。

entries.definition: The flow of something out of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 某物从一处流出的过程或流量。

entries.definition: A hollow or contact point into which something is plugged.
entries.definitionCN: 供插接的凹口或接触点；插座。

entries.definition: A way out of a building or a road.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物或道路的出入口；出口。

entries.definition: A place or system where goods are bought and sold.
entries.definitionCN: 买卖货物的场所或体系；市场。

entries.definition: An opening that lets air or gas escape.
entries.definitionCN: 让空气或气体逸出的口子；通风口。

normalIntro.en: Outlet pairs a Germanic out with the verb let, so every sense keeps the picture of something being allowed to leave.
normalIntro.cn: outlet 把日耳曼语的 out 与动词 let 配在一起，所以每个义项都保留「有东西被放出去」的画面。

normal.en: Outlet is out plus let, so the first picture is something being let out.
normal.cn: outlet 是 out 加 let，所以第一个画面是有东西被放出去。

normal.en: Let here is the old verb for allow, not the rented-room sense of the modern noun.
normal.cn: 这里的 let 是表示「允许」的旧动词，不是现代名词里「出租房」的意思。

normal.en: Inlet uses in instead of out and reverses the direction.
normal.cn: inlet 把 out 换成 in，方向就反了过来。

normal.en: An electrical outlet lets current out of the wiring into a device.
normal.cn: 电源插座让电流从线路里流出来，进入电器。

normal.en: Retail outlet and outlet store keep the commercial sense of goods finding a way out.
normal.cn: retail outlet 与 outlet store 保留了货物找到出路的那层商业含义。

abstract.en: A half-round drain at the foot of a wall, water slipping through it.
abstract.cn: 墙根一个半圆的排水口，水从那里溜出去。

abstract.en: The same hole serves water, current, goods and anger, because all four are things that must go somewhere.
abstract.cn: 同一个口子同时应付水、电流、货物和怒气，因为四者都是必须有个去处的东西。

abstract.en: A blocked outlet turns a drain into a pool, which is what happens when a feeling has nowhere to go.
abstract.cn: 出口一堵，排水沟就变成一摊水；情绪无处可去时也是如此。

examples.en: Water poured from the outlet into the gutter.
examples.cn: 水从排水口流进沟里。

examples.en: The lamp would not work until she found another outlet.
examples.cn: 她找到另一个插座，台灯才亮起来。

examples.en: Running became his outlet after the long working days.
examples.cn: 在漫长的工作日之后，跑步成了他的发泄途径。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凹特莱特」——墙根那个小口子，水一下就流出去了；记住 outlet 是出口、插座。

root: outlet 是英语复合词，由 out（向外，古英语 ūt）加 let（让、放，古英语 lǣtan）构成，本义「让出去的地方」，先指排水口，后扩展到销路、插座与情绪的发泄途径。属日耳曼语材料，拉丁语没有可靠的同族派生词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a point where something is allowed to leave; the senses divide into water and air, electric current, goods, and finally feelings.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「某物被允许离开的那个点」；义项分成水与空气、电流、货物，最后是情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a half-round drain at the base of a wall with water slipping through it.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙根一个半圆形排水口，水正从那里流过去。

branches.en: water running along a brick seam into a drain
branches.cn: 水沿砖缝流进排水口

branches.en: a river mouth widening toward the sea
branches.cn: 河口向海面张开

branches.en: a lamp cord plugged into a wall
branches.cn: 灯线插进墙上的插座

branches.en: a shop sign at the edge of town
branches.cn: 城镇边缘的一家店铺招牌

branches.en: a runner breathing hard on a dark road
branches.cn: 有人在暗路上跑得气喘吁吁

intro.en: The word joins the Germanic adverb out to the old verb let, and the family keeps the direction of something going out.
intro.cn: 这个词把日耳曼语副词 out 接到旧动词 let 上，词族里始终保留「有东西往外走」的方向。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

the mouth of a drain or river
the act or amount of flowing out

definition_zh: 审美的；美学的；有审美情趣的；美学；审美观
definition_en: relating to beauty and the judgment of taste, pleasing in appearance, or the set of principles behind a style
core_image: 美术馆里，一个人退后两步，眯起眼打量整面墙的构图
scene: 展厅里灯光很暗，参观者却迟迟挪不动脚。 The gallery's aesthetic appeal drew crowds even on weekdays.
sceneCN: 这里的 aesthetic 是「审美的」（第 1 个义项：与美感判断有关的）；句意是这家画廊的审美吸引力连工作日都能引来人群。

pos.zh: 形容词：审美的；美学的；悦目的

derivatives.zh: 加 -s 构成，义为「美学（学科）」
由同一希腊词根构成，义为「唯美主义者；审美家」
加 -ally 构成，义为「在审美上；从美学角度」
加 -ism 构成，义为「唯美主义」

senses.title: Relating to beauty and taste
senses.definition: concerned with beauty, art, and judgments of taste rather than with usefulness
senses.definitionCN: 关涉美、艺术与品味判断，而不是实用性的
senses.example: The building has real aesthetic value, even if it is costly to heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼确有美学价值，尽管取暖费用很高。
senses.why: Greek aisthetikos meant 'of sense perception'; the word moved from what the senses take in to the special pleasure of beauty.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aisthetikos 意为「与感官知觉有关的」；这个词从感官接收之物，转到美感带来的特殊愉悦。

senses.title: Pleasing in appearance
senses.definition: attractive or well designed in a way that shows good taste
senses.definitionCN: 在外观上悦目，或设计体现出良好品味
senses.example: The new bridge is aesthetic as well as strong.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新桥既结实又美观。
senses.why: When the adjective describes a thing rather than a study, it means the thing satisfies the taste that the first sense names.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词形容一件东西而不是一门学问时，它指该物满足了第一义项所说的那种品味。

senses.title: A set of principles of style
senses.definition: the ideas about beauty and style that shape a work, a movement, or a person's taste
senses.definitionCN: 塑造一件作品、一个流派或一个人品味的关于美与风格的理念
senses.example: The film's aesthetic owes much to 1970s photography.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的审美风格很大程度上借鉴了七十年代的摄影。
senses.why: As a noun the word names not beauty itself but the system of ideas that decides what counts as beautiful.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，这个词指的不是美本身，而是决定什么算美的那套理念系统。

intro.en: A Greek word about sense perception, made into a German science of beauty and then borrowed by English.
intro.cn: 一个关于感官知觉的希腊词，在德国被造成「美的学问」，随后被英语借走。

items.en: aisthesthai meant to perceive with the senses, to feel or notice something through the body.
items.cn: aisthesthai 意为用感官感知，通过身体去感觉或察觉。

items.en: aisthetikos meant 'of perception', concerned with what can be sensed rather than with pure thought.
items.cn: aisthetikos 意为「与知觉有关的」，关注可被感知之物，而非纯粹思想。

items.en: In the eighteenth century German writers made Aesthetik the name of a new discipline of beauty and art.
items.cn: 十八世纪德国作家把 Aesthetik 用作一门研究美与艺术的新学科之名。

items.en: English borrowed aesthetic from German, first as a term of philosophy and then of art criticism.
items.cn: 英语从德语借入 aesthetic，先作哲学术语，后进入艺术批评。

items.en: Everyday use now allows aesthetic to mean simply pleasing to look at, beyond its technical sense.
items.cn: 今天的日常用法让它超出专业范围，直接表示「看上去悦目」。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek root of perception; the second gathers words about beauty and style.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「知觉」的希腊词根；第二组收关于美与风格的词。

entries.definition: the branch of philosophy that studies beauty
a person who cares greatly about beauty
in terms of beauty or appearance
a drug that removes feeling; same perception root, other prefix
entries.definitionCN: 麻醉剂；同词根但前缀不同，意思相反

entries.definition: relating to art or showing skill in art
showing good judgment in beauty and style
pleasing to the senses; more emotional than aesthetic
entries.definitionCN: 美丽的；比 aesthetic 更带情感

entries.definition: relating to the manner of expression rather than beauty
entries.definitionCN: 风格上的；侧重表达方式

normalIntro.en: The root means perception: aesthetic is about what the senses judge as beautiful.
normalIntro.cn: 词根意为「知觉」：aesthetic 讲的是感官判定为美的东西。

normal.en: The Greek root aisthet- means perceive, so aesthetic is about felt beauty.
normal.cn: 希腊词根 aisthet- 意为「感知」，所以 aesthetic 关乎被感受到的美。

normal.en: An anesthetic removes perception; an aesthetic sharpens it.
normal.cn: anesthetic 去掉知觉，aesthetic 则磨锐知觉。

normal.en: Use aesthetically to describe how something looks.
normal.cn: 用 aesthetically 来描述某物看上去如何。

normal.en: An aesthete is a person who lives for beauty.
normal.cn: an aesthete 是为美而活的人。

normal.en: Spell it with ae-, and keep the th before the final -etic.
normal.cn: 拼写以 ae- 开头，结尾 -etic 前要先写 th。

abstract.en: Picture a visitor stepping back from a wall of paintings to judge the whole arrangement.
abstract.cn: 想象参观者从一整墙画前退后两步，判断整体布局。

abstract.en: See the same judgment applied to a bridge, where strength and shape must agree.
abstract.cn: 想象同一种判断落到一座桥上，强度与形状必须彼此相称。

abstract.en: Imagine the rules behind the judgment written down as a system of taste.
abstract.cn: 想象把判断背后的规则写成一套品味体系。

examples.en: The old factory has little aesthetic value but great historical interest.
examples.cn: 这座旧工厂没什么美学价值，却有很高的历史意义。

examples.en: Her garden is practical rather than aesthetic.
examples.cn: 她的花园重实用胜过美观。

examples.en: The designer explained the film's aesthetic in a short interview.
examples.cn: 设计师在简短访谈中解释了这部电影的审美取向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊斯赛提克」——伊斯在美术馆里退后两步，赛着看谁的品味更高。

root: 希腊语 aisthetikos「与知觉有关的」来自 aisthesthai「感知」；十八世纪德语把它造成研究美的学科名，英语随后借入，兼指「审美的」「悦目的」与「审美观」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses move from the study of beauty, to a thing that satisfies it, to the system of taste behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从研究美的学问，走到满足这种学问的东西，再到它背后的品味体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visitor steps back to judge a whole wall of paintings.
core.cn: 核心意象：参观者退后两步，判断整墙画作。

branches.en: a listed building valued for beauty, not profit
branches.cn: 因美而非因盈利被珍视的登录建筑

branches.en: a question of taste rather than use
branches.cn: 关乎品味而非用途的问题

branches.en: a bridge whose shape pleases the eye
branches.cn: 外形悦目的桥

branches.en: a film borrowing the look of old photography
branches.cn: 借鉴旧摄影外观的电影

branches.en: perception, then pleasure, then the rules of pleasure
branches.cn: 先知觉，再愉悦，最后是愉悦的规则

intro.cn: 一个表示「感知」的希腊动词、它的形容词，加上英语词尾。

latinIntro.cn: 词根是希腊语；拉丁语只把它当作学术借词使用，因此这里不列拉丁词条。

definition_en: to move on hands and knees, to move very slowly, or a fast way of swimming
core_image: 一个婴儿贴在地上，用膝盖和手掌一点点往前挪
scene: 车流堵在路上，只能一米一米地往前挪。 Traffic crawled through the tunnel for an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 crawl 指「缓慢行进」（第 2 个义项：车流几乎走不动地往前挪）；句意是车流在隧道里慢慢挪了一个小时。

senses.title: To move on the ground
senses.definition: to move forward on your hands and knees
senses.definitionCN: 用手和膝盖向前移动
senses.example: The baby crawled across the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿爬过地板。
senses.why: The ground is the first road a body learns.
senses.whyCN: 地面是身体学会的第一条路。

senses.title: To move very slowly
senses.definition: to move very slowly, as traffic does
senses.definitionCN: 像车流那样极慢地移动
senses.example: The queue crawled toward the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍慢慢挪向大门。
senses.why: A crowd in a narrow space moves like one slow animal.
senses.whyCN: 人群挤在窄处，就像一头慢吞吞的动物。

senses.title: The fast swimming stroke
senses.definition: a fast swimming stroke with the face down in the water
senses.definitionCN: 脸朝下、速度最快的一种游泳姿势
senses.example: She swam the crawl across the pool.
senses.exampleCN: 她用自由泳游过了泳池。
senses.why: In water the body lies flat and pulls itself forward.
senses.whyCN: 在水里，身体放平，用手把自己往前拉。

intro.en: Crawl comes from Middle English crawlen, probably from an Old Norse word meaning to claw or scratch.
intro.cn: crawl 源自中古英语 crawlen，很可能来自一个意为用爪抓扒的古诺斯语词。

items.en: Krafla meant to claw or scratch with the hands.
items.cn: krafla 意为用手抓或扒。

items.en: Crawlen meant to move low, pulling with the limbs.
items.cn: crawlen 意为贴低身子、用四肢拉着前进。

items.en: Crawl named the slow creeping of a child.
items.cn: crawl 指孩子缓慢地匍匐前行。

items.en: It widened to slow traffic and to a swimming stroke.
items.cn: 它扩展到缓慢的车流和一种泳姿。

items.en: It now covers babies, queues and the front crawl.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖婴儿、排队的队伍与自由泳。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that rhyme with crawl, and the meaning group names other ways of slow movement.
note.cn: 形近组收集与 crawl 押韵的词，近义组列出其他缓慢移动的说法。

to speak slowly with long vowels
to write in a quick untidy way
to move slowly and quietly

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a baby on the floor, then move to a queue in a tunnel and to a swimmer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从地上的婴儿开始，再到隧道里的车流，最后到游泳的人。

normal.en: Crawl begins with a scratching sound: hands pulling at the ground.
normal.cn: crawl 开头带着抓扒的意味：手在地面上拉。

normal.en: A baby crawls before it walks, because the floor is closer.
normal.cn: 婴儿先爬后走，因为地面更近。

normal.en: Traffic that crawls is a long metal animal with no legs.
normal.cn: 缓慢的车流，是一头没有腿的长金属动物。

normal.en: In the front crawl your arms behave like small oars.
normal.cn: 游自由泳时，两条手臂就像两支小桨。

normal.en: Anything moving an inch a minute is crawling.
normal.cn: 任何一分钟只挪一点点的东西，都在 crawl。

abstract.en: Picture small palms pressed flat on a wooden floor.
abstract.cn: 想象小小的手掌平按在木地板上。

abstract.en: Picture a line of red lights moving one metre at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一串红色尾灯一次只挪一米。

abstract.en: Picture a face turning sideways for a quick breath.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸侧过去快速换气。

examples.en: The child crawled under the table.
examples.cn: 孩子爬到桌子底下。

examples.en: Cars crawled along the flooded road.
examples.cn: 汽车在积水的路上缓慢行驶。

examples.en: He can swim the crawl for an hour.
examples.cn: 他能用自由泳游一个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crawl 记成 cr（抓）加 awl（锥子）：像锥子一样贴着地面，一边抓一边往前。

root: 源自中古英语 crawlen，可能来自古诺斯语 krafla（用爪抓扒），本指贴地用手脚扒着前进，后引申为缓慢移动与一种游泳姿势。

sensesIntro.en: From a body low on the floor to a queue in slow motion and a swimmer pulling water.
sensesIntro.cn: 从贴在地面的身体，到慢动作的车流，最后到划水的泳者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small body close to the ground, pulling itself forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具贴近地面的小身体把自己往前拉。

branches.en: Hands and knees take turns carrying the body.
branches.cn: 手和膝轮流把身体带向前。

branches.en: A long line of cars moves at the speed of a crawl.
branches.cn: 一长串车以爬行的速度前进。

branches.en: In water the same low posture becomes speed.
branches.cn: 在水里，同样的低姿态变成了速度。

branches.en: Slow and low is the shared picture of both.
branches.cn: 又低又慢，是两者共有的画面。

branches.en: One crawl is slow on land and fast in water.
branches.cn: 同一个词，在陆上慢，在水里快。

intro.en: Crawl is a native base word that builds the agent -er, the adjective -y and compounds with space.
intro.cn: crawl 是本族词根，可加 -er 表人、-y 表性质，并与 space 等构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin, with no Latin base behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，背后没有拉丁词基。

items.example: He does ten crawls across the pool.
items.exampleCN: 他在泳池里游十个来回。

items.example: The ant crawled up my arm.

items.meaning: a creature or machine that crawls
items.example: A crawler moved along the pipe.
items.exampleCN: 一台履带机器沿管道移动。
那间黑地窖让人心里发毛。

definition_en: in a way shared by two or more people or groups, who act or are responsible together
core_image: 两只手握在同一支笔上，一起在同一张纸上签名
scene: 两家公司各派一名代表坐在长桌两侧，同时签字。 The flat is owned jointly by the two sisters.
sceneCN: 这里 jointly 是「共同地」（第 1 个义项：由两个或更多方一起做或共有），句意为这套房子由姐妹俩共同拥有。画面里的物件：长桌、代表、签字笔。

pos.zh: 副词：共同地；连带地；联合地

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「联合的；共同的」
基础词名词义，指接合处或关节
joint 与 jointly 的动词来源，义为「连接；加入」

senses.title: Shared by more than one party
senses.definition: in a way that is shared by two or more people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 由两个或更多人或团体共同分享的方式
senses.example: The two families jointly own the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 两个家庭共同拥有这片果园。
senses.why: Jointly marks the sharing of one thing by more than one side.
senses.whyCN: jointly 标出一样东西被不止一方分享。

senses.title: Acting together
senses.definition: by acting together rather than separately
senses.definitionCN: 指一起行动而不是各自行动
senses.example: The police and the council acted jointly on the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 警方和议会在该方案上联合行动。
senses.why: From sharing an object the word moves to sharing an action.
senses.whyCN: 从共有一个东西，这个词转向共做一个动作。

senses.title: Legally liable together
senses.definition: in law, so that the parties share a single liability or right
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指各方共同承担同一份责任或权利
senses.example: They signed jointly and severally for the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为这笔贷款签了连带责任。
senses.why: The legal sense fixes joint liability in one adverb.
senses.whyCN: 法律义用一个副词把连带责任固定下来。

senses.title: Written or produced by two authors
senses.definition: with two or more named authors or makers
senses.definitionCN: 指由两位或更多署名作者共同写出或制作
senses.example: The paper was written jointly by a chemist and a historian.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文由一位化学家和一位历史学家合写。
senses.why: Authorship is another kind of sharing that the adverb labels.
senses.whyCN: 署名是另一种共同分享，这个副词同样能标注。

senses.title: Together in a single arrangement
senses.definition: considered together as one arrangement rather than in parts
senses.definitionCN: 指把几样东西作为一个整体来合计
senses.example: The units are jointly managed by one committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这些单位由同一个委员会共同管理。
senses.why: Managing several things as one unit is the same sharing seen from the institution side.
senses.whyCN: 把几样东西当一个单位来管，是同一份共享从机构角度看的样子。

intro.en: Jointly is joint plus the adverb ending -ly; joint itself comes from Latin junctus through French.
intro.cn: jointly 是 joint 加副词词尾 -ly；joint 本身经由法语来自拉丁语 junctus。

items.en: junctus, the past participle of jungere, meant joined.
items.cn: jungere 的过去分词 junctus 意为「被连接的」。

items.en: Old French joint named a joining or a place where two parts meet.
items.cn: 古法语 joint 指接合，或两部分的相接处。

items.en: English took joint as noun and adjective, meaning a place of meeting and then shared.
items.cn: 英语把 joint 用作名词和形容词，先指相接处，后指共同的。

items.en: The adverb jointly formed with -ly to mark shared action.
items.cn: 副词 jointly 由 -ly 构成，用来标记共同的行为。

items.en: Legal usage fixed the pair jointly and severally.
items.cn: 法律用法固定了 jointly and severally 这一对说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the join stem; the near-meaning group holds adverbs and phrases for shared action.
note.cn: 形近组共用 join 词干；近义组收表示共同行动的副词与说法。

entries.definitionCN: 同源的基础形容词，义为「共同的」或指接合处。

entries.definition: Having joints, as a doll or stem.
entries.definitionCN: 由 joint 加 -ed 构成，义为「有关节的」。

entries.definition: To connect or become a member.
entries.definitionCN: 同源动词，义为「连接；加入」。

In a way felt or done by both sides.

normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语分词走到有两个签名的那份合同。

examples.en: They are jointly responsible for the repairs.
examples.cn: 他们对维修共同负责。

definition_zh: 整夜；一夜之间；过夜的；留宿
definition_en: through the whole night, happening with striking speed, arranged for or lasting one night, or to spend the night in a place
core_image: 凌晨的候车室里长椅上搭着外套，窗外雪还在下
scene: 凌晨的候车室里只剩下几个人，长椅上搭着外套，窗外的雪一直没停。 The letters were flown overnight to the northern office.
sceneCN: 这里 overnight 是「整夜、在夜间」（第 1 个义项：副词，指整个夜里）；句意为信件连夜空运到北方的办事处，画面是凌晨候车室的长椅与不停的雪。

derivatives.zh: 由 overnight 加表示人或行程的后缀 -er 构成，义为「过夜的人；短途过夜行程」
由 overnight 与 bag 复合而成，义为「短途过夜用的小旅行包」

senses.title: Through the whole night
senses.definition: for or during the whole of the night, from evening until morning
senses.definitionCN: 从傍晚到早晨的整段时间里，或贯穿整个夜里
senses.example: We stayed overnight in a small hotel near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站附近一家小旅馆过了夜。
senses.why: The word is over plus night, so its first job is to stretch an action across the dark hours; nothing is quick yet, only continuous.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 over 加 night，最初的作用就是把一个动作拉长、横跨整个黑夜；此时还没有「快」的意思，只有「持续」。

senses.title: With striking speed
senses.definition: used of a change that seems to happen in a single night, so fast that people are caught unprepared
senses.definitionCN: 形容变化快得像只过了一夜，让人来不及准备
senses.example: The book became an overnight success.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书一夜之间成了畅销书。
senses.why: One night is a very short unit for a large change, so naming the night measures the surprise rather than the duration; the shorter the stretch, the more startling the result.
senses.whyCN: 对一场大变化来说，一夜是很短的计量单位，所以说「过了一夜」量的是惊讶程度而不是时长；时间越短，结果越惊人。

senses.title: Arranged for or lasting one night
senses.definition: describing a bag, stay, train or trip that belongs to a single night away from home
senses.definitionCN: 形容行李、逗留、列车或行程属于离家的一个晚上
senses.example: He packed an overnight bag and left before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他收拾了一个过夜的小包，天没亮就走了。
senses.why: Once the adverb marks a night, the same word can stand before a noun and label whatever belongs to that one night, so position becomes a kind of purpose.
senses.whyCN: 副词标出「一夜」之后，同一个词也能站到名词前面，标注属于那一夜的东西；位置义由此转成用途义。

senses.title: To spend the night somewhere
senses.definition: to stay in a place for the night, especially when travelling
senses.definitionCN: 在某处停留一夜，尤指旅行途中
senses.example: He overnighted in the city before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开会前他在城里住了一夜。
senses.why: English turns many time words into verbs when travel needs a short label, and overnight simply means to do the thing the adverb describes: pass the night there.
senses.whyCN: 旅途中需要一个短说法时，英语常把时间词变成动词；overnight 作动词就是照副词所说的去做——在那里过完这一夜。

intro.en: Overnight joins two inherited Germanic words, first as a phrase for a stretch of time and later as an adjective and a verb of travel.
intro.cn: overnight 把两个日耳曼语固有词连在一起，先是表示一段时间跨度的短语，后来成为形容词与旅行动词。

items.en: Over and night both descend from reconstructed Germanic forms, and their union names time rather than place.
items.cn: over 与 night 都上溯到重构的日耳曼语形式，两者结合命名的是时间而不是地点。

items.en: Old English used ofer niht as a phrase for something lasting or happening through the dark hours.
items.cn: 古英语用 ofer niht 这个短语表示贯穿黑夜、或整夜发生的事。

items.en: Middle English wrote the two parts together and used the word for work and travel done between dusk and dawn.
items.cn: 中古英语把两部分合写，用这个词指黄昏到黎明之间完成的工作与行程。

items.en: Steam trains and mail coaches made the attributive use common in overnight bag, overnight train and overnight stay.
items.cn: 蒸汽列车与邮车让定语用法流行起来，出现 overnight bag、overnight train 与 overnight stay 这类说法。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative overnight success and a verb meaning to spend the night.
items.cn: 现代英语补上比喻性的 overnight success，以及表示「过夜」的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived noun, the inflected forms and a compound; the near-meaning group gathers words of nightly time and of sudden change.
note.cn: 形近组收派生名词、各屈折形式与一个复合词；近义组收表示夜间时间与突然变化的词。

entries.definition: A person who stays overnight, or a short trip that lasts one night.
entries.definitionCN: 过夜的人，或只持续一晚的短途行程。

entries.definition: The past form of the verb, meaning stayed for the night.
entries.definitionCN: 动词过去式，意为过了一夜。

entries.definition: The present participle of the verb.
A small bag holding what one needs for one night away.
entries.definitionCN: 装一晚外出所需物品的小包。

entries.definition: Happening every night, or during each night.
entries.definitionCN: 每夜发生的，或在每夜期间发生的。

entries.definition: Quickly and without warning.
Happening immediately, with no delay at all.
Active at night rather than during the day.
entries.definitionCN: 在夜间而非白天活动的。

normalIntro.en: The word is over plus night, and its hooks return to the hours crossed, the surprise of a one-night change, and the bag packed for that night.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 over 加 night，记忆钩子都回到跨过去的那几个小时、一夜之变带来的惊讶，以及为那一夜收拾的包。

normal.en: Overnight is over plus night, so the word crosses a stretch of time rather than a distance.
normal.cn: overnight 是 over 加 night，跨过的是一段时间，而不是一段距离。

normal.en: The earliest use is a phrase, which is why the word still describes duration before it describes speed.
normal.cn: 最早的用法是短语，所以这个词先描述时长，后来才描述速度。

normal.en: The adjective follows the same picture and stands before whatever belongs to that one night, such as a bag or a train.
normal.cn: 形容词沿用同一画面，站在属于那一夜的东西前面，如包或列车。

normal.en: Overnight success measures surprise, not hours, so a fast rise needs only the name of one night.
normal.cn: overnight success 量的是惊讶而不是小时，所以飞快的崛起只需「一夜」这个名字。

normal.en: The verb simply asks someone to do what the adverb says, which is to pass the night in a place.
normal.cn: 动词只是让人照副词所说的去做，就是在某处过完这一夜。

abstract.en: A lit platform at dawn with coats over the benches is the word at its plainest.
abstract.cn: 黎明时亮着灯的站台、长椅上搭着外套，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A single night between two ordinary days shows how a long change can be squeezed into one dark stretch.
abstract.cn: 两个平常日子之间的一夜，显示一场长变化如何被压进一段黑夜。

abstract.en: A small bag by the door is the word turned into an object ready to go.
abstract.cn: 门边一只小包，是这个词变成随时可以带走的物件。

examples.en: We stayed overnight in a small hotel near the station.
examples.cn: 我们在车站附近一家小旅馆过了夜。

examples.en: The book became an overnight success.
examples.cn: 这本书一夜之间成了畅销书。

examples.en: He overnighted in the city before the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会前他在城里住了一夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧沃奈特」——欧沃熬了一整夜，天亮时事情已经变了模样。

root: overnight 由古英语 ofer（越过）与 niht（夜）合成，字面为「越过一夜」；两半都属日耳曼语固有词，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a stretch of time crossed in the dark; the senses move from lasting the whole night, to a change that seems that quick, to whatever belongs to one night, and to the act of staying.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是黑夜里被跨过去的一段时间；义项从持续整夜，转到快得像只过一夜的变化，转到属于那一夜的东西，最后转到过夜这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nearly empty waiting room before dawn, coats over the benches, snow still falling outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：天亮前几乎空了的候车室，外套搭在长椅上，窗外雪还没停。

branches.en: a train running through the dark hours
branches.cn: 在黑夜中一路行驶的列车

branches.en: a book famous by breakfast
branches.cn: 早饭时就已出名的书

branches.en: a small bag packed for one night
branches.cn: 为一夜收拾好的小包

branches.en: a traveller signing a hotel register at midnight
branches.cn: 午夜在旅馆登记簿上签名的旅人

branches.en: one night, once too short to believe and once merely spent
branches.cn: 同一夜，一次短得难以置信，一次只是被度过

intro.en: The word places the Old English word for over before the word for night and then grows a noun, a compound and a set of verb forms.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语中表示「越过」的词放在「夜」前面，随后长出一个名词、一个复合词与一整套动词形式。

latinIntro.en: This is a native Germanic compound with no Latin family; Latin nox is only a distant Indo-European relative of night, not part of this word's descent.
latinIntro.cn: 这是日耳曼语固有复合词，没有拉丁词族；拉丁语 nox 只是 night 的印欧远亲，不属于这个词的传承。

items.meaning: a bag for one night away

definition_en: to force saliva out of the mouth, or a rod for roasting meat
core_image: 一口唾沫落在沙地上
scene: 他吐掉了苦涩的药片。 He spat out the bitter pill.
sceneCN: 这里 spit 是「吐出」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他吐掉了苦涩的药片。

senses.title: Send out saliva
senses.definition: to force saliva out of the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 把唾液从嘴里用力送出
senses.example: He spat on the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 他往地上吐了口唾沫。
senses.why: The basic bodily action is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 最基本的身体动作，是这个词的核心。

senses.title: Spit something out
senses.definition: to send something out of the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 把嘴里的东西吐出来
senses.example: He spat out the bitter pill.
senses.exampleCN: 他吐掉了苦涩的药片。
senses.why: The action takes an object, often something unwanted.
senses.whyCN: 带宾语时指吐出不要的东西。

senses.title: A roasting rod
senses.definition: a thin rod used to hold meat over a fire
senses.definitionCN: 用来把肉架在火上烤的细杆
senses.example: The meat turned slowly on the spit.
senses.exampleCN: 肉在烤肉叉上慢慢转动。
senses.why: The noun names an old cooking tool.
senses.whyCN: 名词义指一种古老的炊具。

intro.en: Spit is an Old English verb for sending out saliva.
intro.cn: spit 是古英语动词，指把唾液送出嘴外。

items.en: Spittan meant to spit.
items.cn: spittan 意为吐唾沫。

items.en: The verb kept the same bodily sense.
items.cn: 这个词保持了相同的身体动作义。

items.en: Spit out extended it to any object in the mouth.
items.cn: spit out 把它扩展到嘴里的任何东西。

items.en: Spit and polish described hard cleaning.
items.cn: spit and polish 形容费力擦洗。

items.en: The noun spit kept the roasting rod sense.
items.cn: 名词 spit 保留了烤肉叉之义。

note.en: Spit is compared with look-alike words and words for the mouth.
note.cn: 把 spit 与形近词以及表示口腔动作的词作比较。

entries.definition: the inner self
a wish to hurt others
to divide into parts
to send out in a rush
to push air out of the throat
to let saliva run from the mouth

normalIntro.en: Spit is the mouth throwing something out.
normalIntro.cn: spit 就是嘴巴把东西扔出去。

normal.en: Don't spit in the street.
normal.cn: 别在街上吐痰。

normal.en: He spat out the seed.
normal.cn: 他把籽吐了出来。

normal.en: Spit it out, what happened?
normal.cn: 快说，发生什么了？

normal.en: The meat turned on the spit.
normal.cn: 肉在烤肉叉上转动。

normal.en: The cat spat at the dog.
normal.cn: 猫冲狗哈气。

abstract.en: Some words are spat, not spoken.
abstract.cn: 有些话是吐出来的，不是说出来的。

abstract.en: A bitter taste is refused by the tongue.
abstract.cn: 苦味会被舌头拒绝。

abstract.en: Fire and spit both turn meat into food.
abstract.cn: 火与烤叉，一起把肉变成食物。

examples.en: He spat on the ground.
examples.cn: 他往地上吐了口唾沫。

examples.en: He spat out the bitter pill.
examples.cn: 他吐掉了苦涩的药片。

examples.en: The meat turned slowly on the spit.
examples.cn: 肉在烤肉叉上慢慢转动。

dict_mnemonic.text: spit 的过去式是 spat；spit out 是「吐出」，spit it out 是「快说出来」，roasting spit 是「烤肉叉」；注意与 spirit、spite 区分。

root: 来自古英语 spittan（吐唾沫），核心义是口腔把东西送出去，名词义「烤肉叉」来自另一条同形词源。

sensesIntro.en: Spit means to send out saliva, to spit something out, or a rod for roasting.
sensesIntro.cn: spit 指吐唾沫、吐出东西，或烤肉叉。

core.en: The mouth pushing matter away.
core.cn: 嘴巴把东西推开。

branches.en: A drop of saliva hits the dust.
branches.cn: 一滴唾液落进尘土。

branches.en: A bitter pill leaves the tongue.
branches.cn: 苦药片离开了舌头。

branches.en: Meat turns above red coals.
branches.cn: 肉在红炭上方转动。

branches.en: Saliva and objects leave by one motion.
branches.cn: 唾液与物件，以同一种动作离开。

branches.en: One spit rejects, the other feeds.
branches.cn: 一个 spit 在拒绝，另一个在供养。

intro.en: Spit forms irregular verb parts and compound nouns.
intro.cn: spit 构成不规则动词形式和复合名词。

latinIntro.en: Spit has no Latin root; it comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: spit 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语。

items.example: The cat is spitting at us.

items.exampleCN: 唾液顺着他的下巴流下。

items.example: He threw a spitball in class.
items.exampleCN: 他在课上扔了个纸团弹。

items.example: An old spittoon stood in the corner.
items.exampleCN: 角落里放着一个旧痰盂。

definition_zh: 能力；官能；院系；全体教员
definition_en: a natural ability or power of mind or body; a department of a university; all the teachers of a university or school
core_image: 一个人身上可以被调用的几项本领，也是一所大学里的几大学院
scene: 她在语言方面很有天赋。 She has a great faculty for languages.
sceneCN: 这里 faculty 是「能力、天赋」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在语言方面很有天赋。

senses.title: A natural ability
senses.definition: a natural ability or power of the mind or body
senses.definitionCN: 心智或身体天生具备的能力
senses.example: He has a faculty for solving puzzles.
senses.exampleCN: 他有解谜的天赋。
senses.why: The base sense is an inner power that can be used.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是可以被调用的内在能力。

senses.title: A university department
senses.definition: a division of a university that groups related subjects
senses.definitionCN: 大学中按相关学科划分的部门
senses.example: She teaches in the faculty of law.
senses.exampleCN: 她在法学院任教。
senses.why: A group of scholars forms a body with its own powers.
senses.whyCN: 一群学者组成拥有自身权能的团体。

senses.title: The teaching staff
senses.definition: all the teachers and researchers of a university or school
senses.definitionCN: 一所大学或学校的全体教师与研究人员
senses.example: The faculty voted for the new rule.
senses.exampleCN: 全体教员投票支持新规定。
senses.why: The department sense extends to the people in it.
senses.whyCN: 院系义延伸到其中的成员。

senses.title: An academic staff member
senses.definition: a member of the teaching or research staff at a university, especially in American English
senses.definitionCN: 大学的教师或研究人员，尤用于美式英语
senses.example: Two faculty attended the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 两名教职员出席了典礼。
senses.why: American usage treats the group word as a count noun for members.
senses.whyCN: 美式英语把这个集合名词用作可数的成员。

intro.en: Faculty comes from Latin facultas, ability or opportunity, from facilis.
intro.cn: faculty 来自拉丁语 facultas（能力、机会），源头是 facilis。

items.en: Facultas means ability or opportunity.
items.cn: facultas 意为能力或机会。

items.en: Facilis means easy to do.
items.cn: facilis 意为容易做的。

items.en: Faculte names a power or branch of learning.
items.cn: faculte 指一种能力或学问分支。

items.en: The word names a division of study.
items.cn: 中世纪大学用该词指学科分部。

items.en: Faculty also means the teaching staff.
items.cn: 现代英语中 faculty 也指全体教员。

note.en: Faculty is an ability or academic body; facility is a place or ease.
note.cn: faculty 是能力或院系，facility 则是设施或便利。

entries.definition: a place or equipment for a purpose
not working correctly
based on facts
the power to do something
a division of an organization
the people who work for an organization

normalIntro.en: Faculty moves from inner powers to the academic body that uses them.
normalIntro.cn: faculty 从内在能力延伸到运用这些能力的学术团体。

normal.en: She has a faculty for making people laugh.
normal.cn: 她有逗人发笑的本事。

normal.en: The faculty of medicine is highly ranked.
normal.cn: 医学院排名很高。

normal.en: The faculty met to discuss the curriculum.
normal.cn: 全体教员开会讨论课程。

normal.en: He lost his mental faculties after the illness.
normal.cn: 病后他丧失了心智能力。

normal.en: Every faculty member received a copy.
normal.cn: 每位教职员都收到了一份。

abstract.en: Picture several switches inside a mind, each a skill.
abstract.cn: 想象头脑里有几个开关，每个对应一种本领。

abstract.en: Imagine a university building named after an ability.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋以能力命名的大学建筑。

abstract.en: Think of teachers gathered as one powerful body.
abstract.cn: 把教师们想成凝聚成的一个有力整体。

examples.en: The faculty of speech develops early in children.
examples.cn: 语言能力在儿童早期发展。

examples.en: She joined the faculty of the university.
examples.cn: 她加入了这所大学的教职。

examples.en: The faculty approved the new programme.
examples.cn: 全体教员批准了新课程。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: faculty 与 facility 同源，都来自「容易、能做」；能做某事的能力，就是 faculty。

root: faculty 源自拉丁语 facultas（能力、机会），来自 facilis（容易的），由「做得到」引申为能力与院系。

sensesIntro.en: Faculty is a natural ability, a university division, the teaching staff, or one of its members.
sensesIntro.cn: faculty 指天生能力、大学院系、全体教员，或其中一位教职员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: inner powers grouped into a learned body.
core.cn: 核心意象：内在能力聚合成一个学术团体。

branches.en: The base sense is an inner ability.
branches.cn: 基础义是内在能力。

branches.en: Scholars group into a department.
branches.cn: 学者组成院系。

branches.en: The group body means all teachers.
branches.cn: 这一团体指全体教师。

branches.en: American usage counts individual members.
branches.cn: 美式用法把成员视作可数个体。

branches.en: A faculty is both a division and its people.
branches.cn: faculty 既是院系也是其中的人。

intro.en: Faculty shares the Latin root of facility and facile.
intro.cn: faculty 与 facility、facile 共用拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin facultas and facilis explain faculty and its related forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facultas 与 facilis 解释了 faculty 及其相关形式。

items.example: Each faculty member has an office.
items.exampleCN: 每位教职员都有办公室。

items.meaning: a meeting of the teaching staff
items.example: The faculty meeting starts at noon.

items.meaning: the law department of a university
items.example: He studies at the faculty of law.
Old age can weaken mental faculties.
items.exampleCN: 年老可能削弱心智官能。

items.example: Ask your faculty adviser for help.

latinEntries.exampleCN: facilis 演变为 facility 与 facile。

definition_en: a small insect that lives in large groups in the ground, or the group of such insects as a kind
core_image: 一条细细的黑线在地板上移动，每一粒都是活的小东西
scene: 厨房地板上留下一粒糖，几只小虫排成一线。 A single ant carried a crumb across the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 ant 是「蚂蚁」（第 1 个义项：单个蚂蚁）；句意为一只蚂蚁把面包屑搬过地板。画面里有地板、糖粒与排成线的蚂蚁。

derivatives.zh: 由 ant 与 hill 复合，义为「蚁丘；蚁巢」
由 ant 与 eater 复合，义为「食蚁兽」
由 ant 与 like 复合，义为「像蚂蚁一样的」

senses.title: A single small insect
senses.definition: a small insect with a thin waist that lives in an organized colony
senses.definitionCN: 腰部细窄、生活在有组织的蚁群中的小型昆虫
senses.example: An ant crawled up the side of the jar.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蚂蚁沿着罐子的侧面往上爬。
senses.why: Old English named the insect with a word probably meaning 'the biter' or 'the cutter', after its jaws.
senses.whyCN: 古英语给这种昆虫的名字，很可能意为「咬的东西」或「切的东西」，取自它的口器。

senses.title: The species or colony as a group
senses.titleCN: 蚁类；蚁群：作为整体的蚂蚁
senses.definition: the insects of this kind considered as a group, or a colony of them
senses.definitionCN: 把这类昆虫作为一个整体来看，或指一个蚁群
senses.example: The ant is one of the strongest creatures for its size.
senses.exampleCN: 就体型而言，蚂蚁是最强壮的生物之一。
senses.why: A single ant is almost meaningless alone; the word often stands for the colony that behaves like one body.
senses.whyCN: 单只蚂蚁几乎没有独立意义；这个词常代表像一具身体那样行动的整个蚁群。

intro.en: Ant is an Old English word whose modern form lost several sounds and gained an n from the article.
intro.cn: ant 是一个古英语词，现代形式丢掉了几个音，又从冠词那里得到了一个 n。

items.en: Ǣmete named the ant, and related forms appear across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: ǣmete 指蚂蚁，相关形式见于多种日耳曼语言。

items.en: The reconstructed form suggests an original meaning such as 'the biter' or 'the cutter', describing the insect's jaws.
items.cn: 重构形式暗示原义可能是「咬的东西」或「切的东西」，描述这种昆虫的口器。

items.en: Middle English used emmet and ampte; the shorter forms gradually displaced the longer ones.
items.cn: 中古英语用 emmet 与 ampte；较短的形式逐渐取代了较长的形式。

items.en: In phrases such as an emmet, the n of the article could be heard as part of the noun, a process called metanalysis.
items.cn: 在 an emmet 这类短语里，冠词的 n 可能被听成名词的一部分，这一过程称为「重新切分」。

items.en: The modern ant is short and plain, and it now appears in compounds such as anthill and anteater.
items.cn: 现代 ant 简短朴素，如今出现在 anthill 与 anteater 等复合词中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that resemble ant in sound; the near-meaning group gathers small social insects and their kin.
note.cn: 形近组收读音与 ant 相近的短词；近义组收小型社会性昆虫及其近亲。

entries.definition: The sister of one's father or mother.
One of the branched horns of a deer.
An animal that feeds mainly on ants.
entries.definitionCN: 主要以蚂蚁为食的动物。

entries.definition: The broad class of small six-legged creatures.
A small pale insect that eats wood and lives in colonies.
entries.definitionCN: 吃木头、群居生活的小型浅色昆虫。

entries.definition: A flying insect that collects nectar and lives in hives.
entries.definitionCN: 采集花蜜、住在蜂巢里的飞行昆虫。

entries.definition: An insect with hard wing cases.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the lost n, the short sound, and the picture of a line of tiny carriers.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子用到丢掉的 n、短促的读音，以及「一列小小搬运工」的画面。

normal.en: Say 'ant': one short syllable, as small as the insect.
normal.cn: 读作「ant」，一个短音节，和那只昆虫一样小。

normal.en: It rhymes with pant and chant, which makes the short a easy to hold.
normal.cn: 它与 pant、chant 押韵，短 a 音很容易记住。

normal.en: The old word was emmet, and the n drifted over from 'an emmet'.
normal.cn: 古词是 emmet，n 是从「an emmet」那里漂过来的。

normal.en: An anthill is an ant hill, and an anteater eats ants; the compounds tell the story.
normal.cn: anthill 是蚂蚁的丘，anteater 是吃蚂蚁的兽；复合词自己会讲故事。

normal.en: One ant is tiny; a colony of ants can carry a whole leaf.
normal.cn: 一只蚂蚁很小，一群蚂蚁却能搬走整片叶子。

abstract.en: The ant is proof that a small body can do large work when it is not alone.
abstract.cn: 蚂蚁证明了：小身体只要不孤单，也能做大事。

abstract.en: We notice the single ant only when it is already a line.
abstract.cn: 我们注意到那只蚂蚁时，它往往已经排成了一条线。

abstract.en: The word is small, and most of what it means is the colony behind it.
abstract.cn: 这个词很小，而它含义的大部分是背后的蚁群。

examples.en: An ant can lift several times its own weight.
examples.cn: 一只蚂蚁能举起自身体重数倍的东西。

examples.en: The ants found the sugar within minutes.
examples.cn: 蚂蚁几分钟内就找到了糖。

examples.en: He watched a line of ants cross the path.
examples.cn: 他看着一列蚂蚁穿过小路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安特」：安特趴在地上看蚂蚁，一看就是一下午。

root: 古英语 ǣmete（蚂蚁），源自日耳曼语，原义可能与「咬、切」有关；现代拼写受冠词重新切分影响。

sensesIntro.en: The word names one small insect and also the colony or kind as a whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词既指一只小昆虫，也指作为整体的蚁群或蚁类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single tiny body moving in a line of identical bodies.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具微小的身体，在由相同身体排成的队列中移动。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL: the first sense is one insect.
branches.cn: 个体线：第一个义项是一只昆虫。

branches.en: THE COLONY: the second sense is the group acting as one.
branches.cn: 群体线：第二个义项是作为一个整体行动的蚁群。

branches.en: THE LINE: one ant becomes visible only as part of a moving line.
branches.cn: 队列线：一只蚂蚁只有成为移动队列的一部分时才显眼。

branches.en: THE LOAD: a single ant carries a crumb, and the colony carries the whole store.
branches.cn: 负重线：单蚁搬一粒屑，蚁群搬整个粮仓。

branches.en: THE KIND: the word can stand for the species as a whole, as in the ant.
branches.cn: 种类线：这个词可代表整个蚁类，如 the ant。

intro.en: Ant forms compounds with hill, eater and like, and with roles inside the colony.
intro.cn: ant 与 hill、eater、like 以及蚁群内的角色构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; the compounds are English, though the second elements may come from Latin or French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语；复合词为英语所造，后半部分可能来自拉丁语或法语。

items.meaning: the mound over an ant colony
items.example: The children stepped over a low anthill.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们跨过一个低矮的蚁丘。

items.meaning: an animal that feeds on ants
items.example: The anteater has a long sticky tongue.
items.exampleCN: 食蚁兽有一条长长的黏舌。

items.example: The robot moved with an antlike gait.
items.exampleCN: 那个机器人以蚂蚁般的步态移动。

items.meaning: a small transparent colony kept for observation
items.meaningCN: 为观察而饲养的小型透明蚁群
items.example: He kept an ant farm on his desk.
items.exampleCN: 他在桌上养了一箱蚂蚁。

items.example: The ant colony moved into the wall.

items.meaning: an ant that gathers food and builds the nest
items.meaningCN: 采集食物、修筑巢穴的蚂蚁
items.example: A worker ant can carry twice its weight.
items.exampleCN: 一只工蚁能负重自身两倍。

items.meaning: the egg-laying female of a colony
items.meaningCN: 蚁群中负责产卵的雌蚁
items.example: The queen ant was hidden deep in the nest.

items.meaning: a stinging ant known for painful bites
items.meaningCN: 以刺痛咬人著称的蚁种
items.example: A fire ant stung his hand.

definition_zh: 尴尬；难堪；令人尴尬的人或事；困境
definition_en: the feeling of being ashamed or awkward; a person or thing that causes this; a difficult situation
core_image: 一圈栏杆合拢，把人困在众人目光中央
scene: 失误被投到大屏幕上，全场安静了一瞬。 A wave of embarrassment swept over the team.
sceneCN: 这里 embarrassment 是「尴尬」（第 01 个义项：羞愧不自在的感受）；句意是一阵尴尬掠过整个团队。

pos.zh: 名词：尴尬；难堪；令人尴尬的人或事；困境

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ment 得到动词，义为「使尴尬」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「令人尴尬的」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「感到尴尬的」

senses.title: The feeling of awkwardness
senses.definition: the uncomfortable feeling of being ashamed or self-conscious
senses.definitionCN: 因羞愧或在人前不自在而产生的不舒服感受
senses.example: A wave of embarrassment swept over the team.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵尴尬掠过整个团队。
senses.why: The noun names the state of being barred in, so embarrassment is the inner experience of having no easy social exit.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名「被栏杆围住」的状态，所以 embarrassment 就是找不到社交出口时的内在体验。

senses.title: A person or thing that causes shame
senses.definition: someone or something that makes a group or person feel ashamed
senses.definitionCN: 让某个群体或个人感到羞耻的人或事物
senses.example: The failed launch was an embarrassment to the company.
senses.exampleCN: 发射失败让公司非常难堪。
senses.why: By a common shift, the cause of the feeling borrows the name of the feeling, so an embarrassing event becomes an embarrassment.
senses.whyCN: 常见的一种转喻是让「感受的原因」借用「感受」的名字，于是令人难堪的事件本身也叫 embarrassment。

senses.title: A difficult situation, often financial
senses.definition: a difficult or complicated situation, especially a financial one
senses.definitionCN: 困难复杂的处境，尤指经济上的拮据
senses.example: The family faced financial embarrassment after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水之后这家人陷入经济困境。
senses.why: The old barrier sense survives as a general trap, so the noun can still mean being stuck in a difficult position.
senses.whyCN: 古老的栏杆义作为「被困住」保留下来，所以这个名词仍能表示陷在困难处境里。

intro.en: Embarrassment is the English noun built from embarrass with the French-derived ending -ment.
intro.cn: embarrassment 是英语在 embarrass 后加源自法语的 -ment 构成的名词。

items.en: Embarrasser meant to block or entangle.
items.cn: embarrasser 意为阻挡、缠住。

items.en: English borrowed embarrass in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入动词 embarrass。

items.en: The ending -ment turned the verb into a noun of state.
items.cn: 词尾 -ment 把动词变成表示状态的名词。

items.en: The social sense of awkwardness became the main meaning.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，社交尴尬义成为主要含义。

items.en: The noun now covers the feeling, its cause and a financial difficulty.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个名词涵盖感受、成因与经济困境。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the embarrass family; the near-meaning group separates shame, humiliation and a difficult position.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 embarrass 词族展开；近义组区分羞耻、羞辱与困难处境。

entries.definition: To make someone feel awkward.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使尴尬」，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: Causing awkwardness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人尴尬的」。

entries.definition: Feeling awkward.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「感到尴尬的」。

entries.definition: A painful sense of having done wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「羞耻」，强调做错事的痛苦。

entries.definition: The experience of being made to look foolish.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「羞辱」，强调被弄得丢脸。

entries.definition: A problem or a hard situation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「困难」，对应本词的经济困境义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the fence image, then let the noun name the feeling, the cause and the trap.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子保留栏杆画面，再让这个名词分别指感受、成因与困境。

normal.en: Embarrassment is the state of being barred in.
normal.cn: embarrassment 就是被栏杆围住的状态。

normal.en: Embarrass plus -ment makes the noun.
normal.cn: embarrass 加 -ment 构成名词。

normal.en: An embarrassing event is itself called an embarrassment.
normal.cn: 令人难堪的事件本身也叫 embarrassment。

normal.en: Financial embarrassment means being trapped by money trouble.
normal.cn: financial embarrassment 指被钱的问题困住。

normal.en: An embarrassment of riches means too many good choices.
normal.cn: an embarrassment of riches 指好选择太多反而难办。

abstract.en: Picture a spotlight and a fence arriving at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象聚光灯与栅栏同时落到一个人身上。

abstract.en: The noun can name the feeling, the event or the trap.
abstract.cn: 这个名词既能指感受，也能指事件或困境。

abstract.en: Embarrassment is a room with the door blocked.
abstract.cn: embarrassment 就是一间门被堵住的房间。

examples.en: A wave of embarrassment swept over the team.
examples.cn: 一阵尴尬掠过整个团队。

examples.en: The failed launch was an embarrassment to the company.
examples.cn: 发射失败让公司非常难堪。

examples.en: The family faced financial embarrassment after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水之后这家人陷入经济困境。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一摸白肉死门特」——当众被围住，门都找不到

root: 由动词 embarrass 加 -ment 构成；embarrass 经法语 embarrasser 来自 imbarrare，字面为「用栏杆围住」。

sensesIntro.en: Embarrassment names the awkward feeling, the thing that causes it, and the difficult position it leaves behind.
sensesIntro.cn: embarrassment 既指尴尬的感受，也指造成尴尬的事物，还指它留下的困难处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fence closing around someone under a spotlight.
core.cn: 核心意象：聚光灯下，一圈栏杆在某人周围合拢。

branches.en: THE FEELING: the inner side of the barrier.
branches.cn: 感受线：栏杆在内心的那一面。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: an event that puts others behind the barrier.
branches.cn: 成因线：把别人也围进去的事件。

branches.en: THE TRAP: money trouble as a practical fence.
branches.cn: 困境线：金钱难题作为现实中的栏杆。

branches.en: FEELING AND CAUSE: the noun names both.
branches.cn: 感受与成因：同一个名词兼指两者。

branches.en: INNER AND OUTER: a state of mind and a state of affairs.
branches.cn: 内外相通：既可指心理状态，也可指现实处境。

intro.en: Embarrassment is embarrass plus -ment, a noun ending that names a state or result.
intro.cn: embarrassment 是 embarrass 加 -ment，这个词尾表示状态或结果。

latinIntro.en: The -ment ending came into English through French, while the root barra is Romance.
latinIntro.cn: -ment 词尾经法语进入英语，词根 barra 则属于罗曼语族。
