definition_en: a woman who leads a meeting, a committee or a company
core_image: 坐在长桌首席、掌控全场节奏的女性
scene: 她走上台，全场立即安静下来。 The chairwoman thanked every guest.
sceneCN: 这里 chairwoman 指「女主席」（第 1 个义项：会议的女主持人）；句意是女主席向每位来宾致谢。

senses.title: A woman leading a meeting
senses.definition: a woman who controls the order of a meeting and keeps it on time
senses.definitionCN: 掌控会议程序、使会议按时进行的女性
senses.example: The chairwoman opened the discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 女主席宣布讨论开始。
senses.why: The word places chair, the leader seat, beside woman, so it names a woman in that seat.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表示领导座位的 chair 放在 woman 旁边，指坐那个座位的女性。

senses.title: A woman heading a company
senses.definition: the most senior woman officer who leads the board of a company
senses.definitionCN: 领导公司董事会的最高女性负责人
senses.example: The chairwoman approved the new budget.
senses.exampleCN: 女董事长批准了新预算。
senses.why: A board is led from the same head seat, so the title travels from the meeting room into the company.
senses.whyCN: 董事会同样由首席之座来领导，于是这个头衔从会议室走进了公司。

intro.en: Chairwoman combines the old seat of authority with the word for a woman, a pattern borrowed from chairman.
intro.cn: chairwoman 把古老的权威之座与表示女性的词结合，这一构造借自 chairman。

items.en: Cathedra named a formal seat of authority.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cathedra 指权威的正式座位。

items.en: Old French chaire gave English chair.
items.cn: 古法语 chaire 给英语提供了 chair。

items.en: Chairman establishes the pattern of seat plus person.
items.cn: chairman 确立了「座位加人」的构词模式。

items.en: Chairwoman appears when women begin to lead committees publicly.
items.cn: 十九世纪女性开始公开领导委员会时出现 chairwoman。

items.en: The word sits beside chairman and the neutral chairperson.
items.cn: 这个词与 chairman 以及中性的 chairperson 并列使用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the chair compounds, while the meaning group lists other women or leaders in charge.
note.cn: 形近组收集 chair 的复合词，近义组列出其他女性或机构负责人说法。

entries.definition: the leading seat or office
a man who leads a meeting
a neutral word for the leader
the head of a company or country
entries.definitionCN: 公司或国家的最高负责人

entries.definition: a senior member of a board
the person who guides a group

normalIntro.en: These hooks read the word as woman plus chair and connect it to the boardroom.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把词读成 woman 加 chair，并与董事会场景相连。

normal.en: Woman plus chair: the woman who holds the leading seat leads the meeting.
normal.cn: woman 加 chair：握住首席之位的女性就领导这场会议。

normal.en: The chairwoman of the board speaks before the other directors.
normal.cn: the chairwoman of the board 在其他董事之前发言。

normal.en: Vice chairwoman and acting chairwoman mark the deputy and the stand-in.
normal.cn: vice chairwoman 与 acting chairwoman 分别标记副手与代理人。

normal.en: Chairperson avoids marking gender, and chairwoman marks it clearly.
normal.cn: chairperson 不标记性别，chairwoman 则明确标记。

normal.en: To elect a chairwoman is to choose the woman who will sit at the head.
normal.cn: elect a chairwoman 就是选出将坐首席的那位女性。

abstract.en: Picture a woman standing as the room goes quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象一位女性站起时全场安静下来。

abstract.en: Picture a name plate reading chairwoman at the head of the table.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌首席的名牌上写着女主席。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to call the first vote of the year.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起，宣布今年的第一次表决。

examples.en: The chairwoman welcomed the new members.
examples.cn: 女主席欢迎新成员。

examples.en: She became chairwoman of the company in May.
examples.cn: 她在五月成为公司董事长。

examples.en: The chairwoman asked the board to vote.
examples.cn: 女主席请董事会进行表决。

dict_mnemonic.text: chair 是首席椅子，woman 是女性：坐在首席上的女性就是女主席。

root: 由 chair（座位、主席职位）加 woman（女性）构成，构词模式来自 chairman。

sensesIntro.en: The meeting sense comes first, and the same word extends to the woman who heads a company board.
sensesIntro.cn: 会议义先出现，同一个词又扩展到领导公司董事会的女性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a woman seated at the head of the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：坐在长桌首席的那位女性。

branches.en: The meeting sense keeps the live work of running a session.
branches.cn: 会议义保留主持一场会议的实际工作。

branches.en: The company sense widens the role to a board.
branches.cn: 公司义把这一角色扩大到董事会。

branches.en: Both depend on one woman holding the leading seat.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖一位女性占据领导之座。

branches.en: Voting and order belong to the meeting sense.
branches.cn: 表决与秩序属于会议义。

branches.en: Budgets and board decisions belong to the company sense.
branches.cn: 预算与董事会决议属于公司义。

intro.en: Chairwoman shares the chairman pattern and also builds chairmanship, its office noun.
intro.cn: chairwoman 与 chairman 同一构词模式，也构成表示职位的 chairmanship。

latinIntro.en: The chair inside the word descends from Latin cathedra, a seat of authority.
latinIntro.cn: 词中的 chair 源自拉丁语 cathedra，即权威之座。

items.meaning: a woman who leads a meeting or board
items.meaningCN: 领导会议或董事会的女性

items.exampleCN: 她的主席任期持续了三年。

items.meaningCN: 男性或通用的主席说法

latinEntries.example: Sedes also meant a seat in Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sedes 在拉丁语中也指座位。

definition_en: completely and entirely, with no part left out and nothing held back
core_image: 一整桶水倒过来，一滴不剩全倒进盆里
scene: 她把桶整个翻过来，水全倒进盆里，桶底一滴也不剩。 I wholly agree with your second point.
sceneCN: 这里 wholly 是「完全地」（第 1 个义项：没有一点遗漏、没有保留）；句意为我完全同意你的第二点。那只被整个翻过来、一滴不剩的水桶，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: To the last part
senses.definition: in every part, so that nothing at all is excluded
senses.definitionCN: 在每一个部分上都是如此，没有任何东西被排除在外
senses.example: I wholly agree with your second point.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全同意你的第二点。
senses.why: The adverb simply says that the complete object is involved, not a part of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是说明涉及的是完整的对象，而不是它的一部分。

senses.title: Entirely, before an adjective
senses.definition: used to strengthen an adjective, meaning quite or utterly
senses.definitionCN: 用于加强形容词，意为「相当」「完全」
senses.example: The whole plan was wholly unexpected to the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 整个计划对员工来说完全出乎意料。
senses.why: Placed before an adjective it works like an intensifier, wiping out the middle ground.
senses.whyCN: 放在形容词之前，它起加强作用，把中间地带抹掉。

senses.title: Not partly
senses.definition: in a negative sentence, used to mean not completely, often with a hint of doubt
senses.definitionCN: 在否定句中表示「不完全」，常带一点保留或怀疑
senses.example: I am not wholly sure that the date is right.
senses.exampleCN: 我并不十分确定日期是对的。
senses.why: A plain no would be too hard, and the word lets a little room into the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 直截了当地否定太生硬，这个词给句子留出一点余地。

senses.title: Owned by one party
senses.definition: in business use, describing a company owned in full by another
senses.definitionCN: 在商业用法中，描述一家公司被另一方全部持有
senses.example: The factory is wholly owned by the parent company in Shanghai.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂由上海的母公司全资拥有。
senses.why: The same idea of completeness moved into company records, where shares are either all or part.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「完整」的想法进入了公司账目，因为股份要么全部要么部分。

intro.en: Wholly is whole plus the adverb ending -ly, made from Old English hal, sound and complete.
intro.cn: wholly 是 whole 加副词词尾 -ly，其源头是表示健全、完整的古英语 hal。

items.en: Hal meant sound and healthy, and the adverb halice meant in a sound or complete way.
items.cn: hal 表示健全、健康，副词 halice 表示以健全或完整的方式。

items.en: With the added w in whole, the adverb appeared as holliche and later wholy.
items.cn: 随着 whole 加入 w，副词写作 holliche，之后又变为 wholy。

items.en: The spelling settled as wholly, keeping the l of whole before the ending.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 wholly，在词尾前保留了 whole 的 l。

items.en: Its chief work became strengthening adjectives such as wholly different and wholly unexpected.
items.cn: 它主要的用途变成加强 wholly different、wholly unexpected 这类形容词。

items.en: Business writing gave it the fixed use of full ownership, as in wholly owned.
items.cn: 商业写作给了它「全资」这一固定用法，如 wholly owned。

note.en: The first group gathers adverbs of completeness that look or sound alike, the second the words that stress a whole without parts.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的「完全」类副词，第二组收强调整体无部分之分的词。

entries.definition: The adjective this adverb is built from.
Sacred, pronounced almost the same.
Full of holes, spelled differently.
Selling in bulk, built on the same base.
In every part, the everyday choice.
As a whole, often before a negative.
To the extreme, with strong feeling.

normalIntro.en: Wholly looks like holy and holey, so the doubled l and the meaning of the base word are the two things to hold on to.
normalIntro.cn: wholly 看着像 holy 和 holey，所以抓住两件事：双写的 l，以及原词「完整」的意思。

normal.en: Whole plus ly means in a complete way, and the l doubles before the ending.
normal.cn: whole 加 ly 表示以完整的方式，加词尾时 l 要双写。

definition_en: a natural desire for food, or a strong interest in something
core_image: 闻到厨房香味时咽下的口水
scene: 锅盖一掀，热气冲上脸，他立刻觉得饿了。 The smell of bread gave him an appetite.
sceneCN: 这里 appetite 是「食欲」（第 1 个义项：对食物的自然欲望）；句意是面包的香味让他有了食欲。

senses.title: A desire for food
senses.definition: the natural feeling that makes you want to eat
senses.definitionCN: 使人想吃东西的自然感觉
senses.example: The smell of bread gave him an appetite.
senses.exampleCN: 面包的香味让他有了食欲。
senses.why: Latin appetitus came from appetere, 'to seek after', built from ad, 'to', and petere, 'to seek'; hunger is the body seeking food.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appetitus 来自 appetere「追寻」，由 ad「向」与 petere「寻求」构成；饥饿就是身体在追寻食物。

senses.title: A strong interest in something
senses.definition: a keen desire for an activity, a challenge, or a type of experience
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动、挑战或某种体验的强烈渴望
senses.example: She has an appetite for risk.
senses.exampleCN: 她喜欢冒险。
senses.why: The seeking after food widened to any object the mind reaches for, so appetite can name ambition or curiosity.
senses.whyCN: 对食物的追寻扩展到心里想抓取的任何对象，所以 appetite 也能指抱负或好奇心。

intro.en: Appetite goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to seek after'.

senses.title: A lack of order

items.cn: ordo 指行列、等级或排列。

items.en: Dis- before a noun marked the loss of that arrangement.
items.cn: 名词前的 dis- 标出这种排列的失去。

items.en: Desordre meant confusion and lack of order.
items.cn: 古法语 desordre 指杂乱与失序。

items.en: English used it for a broken arrangement of things.
items.cn: 英语用来指事物排列被打乱。

items.en: Medicine gave it the sense of a body system out of step.
items.cn: 医学又给了它身体系统失调这一义。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on order, and the meaning group names other states of confusion.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 order 构成，近义组列出别的混乱状态。

entries.definition: an arrangement or a command
not working in a normal way
noisy and hard to control
a state of complete confusion
a state where nothing is clear
a problem of the body or mind

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a chair on its back and end with a body out of rhythm.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一把翻倒的椅子开始，落到一具失去节奏的身体。

normal.en: Dis- plus order: order is gone.
normal.cn: dis 加 order，秩序没了。

normal.en: One fallen chair is an accident; ten are a disorder.
normal.cn: 一把椅子倒下是意外，十把倒下就是混乱。

normal.en: A desk in disorder hides the one paper you need.
normal.cn: 乱桌上总藏着你要的那一张纸。

normal.en: A sleep disorder is a clock inside the body gone wrong.
normal.cn: 睡眠失调，是身体里的钟走错了。

normal.en: Disorder in a street is a matter for the police.
normal.cn: 街上的秩序混乱，要交给警察。

abstract.en: Picture ten chairs lying on their sides.
abstract.cn: 想象十把椅子侧倒在地上。

abstract.en: Picture papers spread from desk to door.
abstract.cn: 想象纸页从桌边铺到门口。

abstract.en: Picture a clock with hands moving at odd speeds.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟的指针快慢失常。

examples.en: The room was left in complete disorder.
examples.cn: 房间被弄得一片混乱。

examples.en: He is being treated for a sleep disorder.
examples.cn: 他正在接受睡眠失调的治疗。

examples.en: The storm threw the whole schedule into disorder.
examples.cn: 暴风雨把整个日程打乱了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disorder 记成「没有次序」：dis 是否定，order 是秩序；东西不在次序里就是混乱，身体里的次序乱了就是失调。

root: 由否定前缀 dis- 加名词 order 构成；order 来自拉丁语 ordo（行列、排列），经古法语 ordre 进入英语。本义是排列被打乱，后来医学又用它指身体或精神系统失去正常节律。

sensesIntro.en: From a room out of order to a body out of step with itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个失序的房间，到一具与自身节奏错开的身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: chairs on their backs and papers across the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：椅子翻倒，纸页铺满地面。

branches.en: The first sense is the room that has lost its plan.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是失去布局的房间。

branches.en: The second sense is the body that has lost its rhythm.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是失去节律的身体。

branches.en: Both senses describe a system without its usual order.
branches.cn: 两个义项都形容失去平常秩序的系统。

branches.en: Both can be caused by one sudden event.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能由一件突发的事引起。

branches.en: Only the second sense is treated by a doctor.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项由医生处理。

intro.en: Disorder stands opposite order, inside the Latin ordo family of rows and ranks.
intro.cn: disorder 与 order 相对，属于拉丁语 ordo（行列与等级）一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ordo, a row or arrangement, gives order; the prefix dis- removes the arrangement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ordo（行列、排列）给出 order，前缀 dis- 把排列拿走。

items.example: A disorderly crowd filled the square.
items.exampleCN: 一群喧闹失控的人挤满广场。

items.example: The disorderliness of the desk was famous.
items.exampleCN: 那张桌子的凌乱很出名。

items.example: An ordered row of jars stood on the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 架子上排着一列整齐的罐子。

items.example: She reordered the shelves by height.
items.exampleCN: 她按高度重新排了架子。

items.example: The queue moved in an orderly way.

definition_en: the basic laws of a country, the way something is made up, or a person's health
core_image: 一本薄薄的册子，写着国家如何运转
scene: 开学第一课，老师讲国家的基本大法。 The constitution limits the power of the government.
sceneCN: 这里 constitution 指「宪法」（第 1 个义项：国家的根本大法）；句意是宪法限制政府的权力。

senses.title: The basic law
senses.definition: the set of rules that a country is governed by
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家据以治理的根本规则
senses.example: The constitution protects freedom of speech.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法保护言论自由。
senses.why: A nation needs one page that other pages must obey.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家需要一页让其他各页都必须服从的文字。

senses.title: How something is made
senses.definition: the way the parts of something are put together
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的各个部分拼合的方式
senses.example: Scientists studied the constitution of the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家研究了土壤的构成。
senses.why: To know a thing you must know what holds it together.
senses.whyCN: 要认识一件事物，就得知道是什么把它拢在一起。

senses.title: A person's build
senses.definition: the natural health and strength of a body
senses.definitionCN: 身体天生的健康与强健程度
senses.example: He has a strong constitution and rarely falls ill.
senses.exampleCN: 他体质强健，很少生病。
senses.why: The same word that builds a state also builds a body.
senses.whyCN: 搭建国家的那同一个词，也用来搭建身体。

intro.en: Constitution comes from Latin constitutio, a setting in order, from constituere, to set up, built on com- and statuere, to place.
intro.cn: constitution 来自拉丁语 constitutio，意为安排、规定，源自 constituere（设立），由 com- 与 statuere（放置）构成。

items.en: Statuere meant to place something so that it stands.
items.cn: statuere 意为把某物放好使它立住。

items.en: Constitutio named the way a thing was ordered and arranged.
items.cn: constitutio 指事物被安排与组织的方式。

items.en: Roman writers used it for an official decree.
items.cn: 罗马作家用它指官方的法令。

items.en: French constitution carried the sense of a settled arrangement.
items.cn: 法语 constitution 带有既定安排的含义。

items.en: English constitution first meant the makeup of body or mind.
items.cn: 英语 constitution 最初指身体或心智的构造。

items.en: It became the standard word for a nation's fundamental law.
items.cn: 它成为指国家根本大法的标准用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin statu- base, and the meaning group names other words for a founding set of rules.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语 statu- 词基，近义组列出其他表示立国规则的词。

entries.definition: to make up or formally establish something
a part that helps form a whole
an established organization or custom
a formal document granting rights
a rule that a society must obey
the way parts are arranged together

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from one thin book of rules, then move to the way parts are fitted and to the strength of a body.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一本薄薄的规则册子开始，再到部件拼合的方式，最后到身体的强健。

normal.en: Con- is together and stitute is set up, so a constitution is everything set up together as one order.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，stitute 是设立，constitution 就是被一起立成一套秩序的东西。

normal.en: The nation's rulebook fits into one pocket.
normal.cn: 整个国家的规则手册，能放进一个口袋。

normal.en: The constitution of a soil and of a state use the same word for a reason.
normal.cn: 土壤的构成与国家的宪法用同一个词，是有原因的。

normal.en: A strong constitution keeps a body running without complaint.
normal.cn: 强健的体质让身体不吭声地运转。

normal.en: Ask what it is made of, and you are asking about its constitution.
normal.cn: 问它由什么构成，问的就是它的构成。

abstract.en: Picture a small book placed above all other books.
abstract.cn: 想象一本小书被放在所有其他书上头。

abstract.en: Picture a wall with every brick named in a plan.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙，每块砖都在图纸上有名字。

abstract.en: Picture a body walking uphill without stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一个身体走上坡路而不停下。

examples.en: The new constitution was approved by a wide margin.
examples.cn: 新宪法以很大优势获得通过。

examples.en: The constitution of the committee changed last year.
examples.cn: 委员会的构成去年发生了变化。

examples.en: Years of running gave her a tough constitution.
examples.cn: 多年跑步让她有了强健的体质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 constitution 记成 con（一起）加 stitute（设立）加 ion：把一个国家的根本规则一起立起来，就是宪法。

root: 源自拉丁语 constitutio（安排、规定），词根 constituere 由 com（一起）与 statuere（放置）构成，本义是一起立定，后指宪法、构成与体质。

sensesIntro.en: From one book of rules, to the fit of parts inside a thing, and to the build of a living body.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一本规则之书，到事物内部部件的拼合，最后到活人身体的底子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin book that all other rules must answer to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本薄书，其他一切规则都要向它交代。

branches.en: The first sense is the rulebook that outranks every other rule.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是压过其他一切规则的规则书。

branches.en: The second sense asks how the parts of a thing are arranged.
branches.cn: 第二个义项问的是一件事物的部件如何排布。

branches.en: The third sense applies the same idea to a living body.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把同一个想法用到活人身上。

branches.en: Both senses describe a whole held together by an inner order.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述靠内在秩序拢住的整体。

branches.en: A body and a state are both judged by how well they are built.
branches.cn: 身体与国家都要看底子搭得好不好。

intro.en: Constitution is built on Latin con-, together, plus statuere, to place, with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: constitution 由拉丁语 con-（一起）、statuere（放置）与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin place base stitut- also appears in constitute, institute and substitute.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的放置词基 stitut- 也出现在 constitute、institute 与 substitute 中。

items.meaning: the settled order of a state or a thing
items.meaningCN: 国家或事物既定的秩序
items.example: The constitution was signed in the hall.
items.exampleCN: 宪法在那座大厅里签署。

items.meaning: to set parts up into a whole

items.exampleCN: 他们提出了宪法层面的诉求。

items.meaning: in a way that follows the basic law
items.exampleCN: 这一举措在宪法上站得住。

items.example: The court struck down the unconstitutional rule.
items.exampleCN: 法院废除了那条违宪的规定。

items.meaning: a part that builds a whole
items.exampleCN: 每个组成部分各有一票。

items.meaning: to put a system in place
items.exampleCN: 他们设立了一套审查程序。

items.example: The statute took effect in May.

definition_zh: 不整洁的；凌乱的；不修边幅的；条理不清的
definition_en: not neat, with things out of their proper places
core_image: 书桌上纸、笔、杯子挤成一堆
scene: 考完试的房间里，卷子摊在床上，袜子挂在椅背上。 Her desk stays untidy even when she has no homework.
sceneCN: 这里 untidy 是「凌乱的」（第 1 个义项：东西没放回原处）；句意为她即便没有作业，书桌也总是乱糟糟的。桌上纸笔杯子堆成一团的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「凌乱地；潦草地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「凌乱；不整洁」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「整洁的」
肯定形式加 -ly，义为「整齐地」

senses.title: Things left out of their proper places
senses.definition: with objects scattered about instead of being put away
senses.definitionCN: 东西散放着而没有收归原处
senses.example: The kitchen was untidy after the family dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 一家人吃过饭后厨房乱成一团。
senses.why: The prefix means not and the base means neat and in good order, so untidy begins as the plain opposite of tidy.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示「不」，词根本义是「整齐、有条理」，因此 untidy 起初就是 tidy 的简单反面。

senses.title: A person careless about appearance
senses.definition: used of someone whose clothes and hair are not looked after
senses.definitionCN: 形容衣着头发不加打理的人
senses.example: He came to the interview looking untidy.
senses.exampleCN: 他来面试时一副不修边幅的样子。
senses.why: What is true of a room is also true of clothing: things are not put where they belong.
senses.whyCN: 房间如此，衣着也如此：东西都没待在它该在的位置上。

senses.title: Writing that is hard to read
senses.definition: used of handwriting or work that is messy on the page
senses.definitionCN: 形容字迹或版面上乱糟糟的
senses.example: Her untidy notes were hard to copy.
senses.exampleCN: 她潦草的笔记很难抄。
senses.why: Ink spread over a page without a line is the same clutter, moved from a room to a sheet of paper.
senses.whyCN: 一笔笔墨落在纸上不成行，就是同一种杂乱，只不过从房间搬到了纸面。

senses.title: Thinking or a plan without order
senses.definition: used of ideas or plans that lack a clear structure
senses.definitionCN: 形容想法或计划缺少清晰结构
senses.example: The untidy argument lost the reader halfway.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论证条理不清，读到一半就跟丢了。
senses.why: If objects can sit out of place, so can the steps of a thought, and this abstract sense follows directly.
senses.whyCN: 既然物件能不在原位，思绪的步骤也可以，这层抽象义就是这样顺势而来的。

senses.title: A situation that looks poorly managed
senses.titleCN: 不整齐的；显得没管好的
senses.definition: used of a business or process that looks badly organised
senses.definitionCN: 形容生意或流程显得管理不善
senses.example: The shop looked untidy and understaffed on a Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店星期六看上去乱糟糟的，人手也不够。
senses.why: A trade that is not kept in order looks untidy, just as a room does.
senses.whyCN: 一桩没人打理的生意看上去乱糟糟，这和一间房的道理一样。

intro.en: A native negative prefix on an adjective that goes back to an old word for time.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在一个可追溯至古老「时间」词的形容词上。

items.en: The prefix un- is native and turns a word into its opposite.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 为英语本土成分，把一个词翻成反义。

items.en: Tid meant time or season, and the adjective tidlic meant timely or in good season.
items.cn: tid 意为「时间、时令」，形容词 tidlic 意为「及时的、合时令的」。

items.en: Tidy shifts from timely to neat, and its spelling settles in this period.
items.cn: tidy 从「及时」转为「整洁」，拼写也在这一时期定型。

items.en: Untidy appears with the sense of things out of order and leaves the old time sense behind.
items.cn: untidy 出现时已是「东西乱了次序」的意思，旧有的时间义被丢掉。

items.en: The word extends to dress, handwriting, and plans that show no order.
items.cn: 此后这个词扩展到衣着、字迹以及毫无条理的计划。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the tidy family and similar un- spellings, while the near-meaning group collects messy words.
note.cn: 形近组沿 tidy 词族及相似的 un- 拼写展开，近义组汇集表示杂乱的说法。

entries.definition: neat and in order
in a neat way
neatness
in a messy way
not firm or stable
entries.definitionCN: 不稳的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: dirty and badly arranged
lacking order
dirty and untidy in appearance
clean and in order

normalIntro.en: The word is the familiar negative of an everyday adjective, and its history lies in an old word for time.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日常形容词的常见否定形式，其历史藏在一个古老的「时间」词里。

normal.en: Un- plus tidy: the positive word means neat and in order.
normal.cn: un- 加 tidy：肯定形式意为整齐有序。

normal.en: An untidy room and an untidy desk are the most frequent collocations.
normal.cn: an untidy room 与 an untidy desk 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Tidy itself once meant timely, which explains why neat things are in season.
normal.cn: tidy 本义为「合时令」，这解释了为什么整洁东西总在恰当的时候出现。

normal.en: The noun is untidiness, the adverb untidily.
normal.cn: 名词是 untidiness，副词是 untidily。

normal.en: Messy is more spoken, untidy more neutral in writing.
normal.cn: messy 更口语，untidy 在书面中更中性。

abstract.en: See a desk with papers sliding into a pile.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，纸片一点点滑成一堆。

abstract.en: Notice a tie worn with a shirt that is not ironed.
abstract.cn: 注意一条领带配着没熨平的衬衫。

abstract.en: Hear a drawer being pushed shut on clothes that will not fit.
abstract.cn: 听抽屉被硬推着关上，衣服塞不进去。

examples.en: His room is always untidy, with books on the floor.
examples.cn: 他的房间总是很乱，书都摊在地上。

examples.en: She came to the meeting looking untidy and out of breath.
examples.cn: 她来开会时一副不修边幅、气喘吁吁的样子。

examples.en: The untidy handwriting made the list hard to read.
examples.cn: 潦草的字迹让这份名单很难辨认。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺太脏」——屋里东西堆得乱，自己也不好意思，只能承认俺这屋实在太乱。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ tidy（整洁的），tidy 源自中古英语 tidy，再往上为古英语 tid（时间、时令）加上形容词词尾 -y，本义「合时令的」

sensesIntro.en: One core state, objects outside their proper place, spreads from rooms to clothes, writing, plans, and business.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个核心状态「东西不在原位」，从房间蔓延到衣着、字迹、计划与生意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk where papers, pens, and cups have piled up.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸、笔与杯子在桌上堆成一团。

branches.en: The room branch: things never got put back.
branches.cn: 房间分支：东西一直没收回去。

branches.en: The person branch: clothes and hair left as they are.
branches.cn: 人物分支：衣着头发都随它去。

branches.en: The page branch: letters that will not stand in line.
branches.cn: 页面分支：字母站不成行。

branches.en: The mind branch: steps of a plan in no fixed order.
branches.cn: 思路分支：计划步骤没有固定次序。

branches.en: The business branch: a process nobody has organised.
branches.cn: 经营分支：没人管过流程的事。

intro.en: A native negative prefix over an adjective whose root once named a point in time.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在一个词根曾指「时节」的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic rather than Latin; the closest Latin idea is tempus, time.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根属日耳曼语而非拉丁语；概念上最近的拉丁词是 tempus（时间）。

items.example: Tid survives in the word tidings.
items.exampleCN: tid 仍存在于 tidings 一词中。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.example: Papers lay untidily on the floor.
